1	// Read-only usage summary for an explicit Agent Team SQLite copy.
2	// This intentionally folds raw Inbox deltas instead of current ledger replay so old channel records remain measurable.
3	import { DatabaseSync } from 'node:sqlite'
4	
5	const QUEUE_THRESHOLD = 8
6	const DAY_MS = 86400000
7	const jsonOutput = process.argv.includes('--json')
8	const databasePath = process.argv.slice(2).find(argument => !argument.startsWith('--'))
9	
10	if (databasePath === undefined) {
11	  console.error('Usage: node --import tsx scripts/team-performance/team-live-usage.ts <ledger-copy.sqlite> [--json]')
12	  process.exit(2)
13	}
14	
15	interface Operation {
16	  readonly sequence: number
17	  readonly occurredAt: string
18	  readonly kind: string
19	  readonly actor?: { readonly kind?: string; readonly memberId?: string; readonly handle?: string }
20	  readonly data?: Record<string, any>
21	}
22	
23	interface Member {
24	  readonly memberId: string
25	  readonly state?: string
26	}
27	
28	function readOperations(path: string): Operation[] {
29	  const database = new DatabaseSync(path, { readOnly: true })
30	  try {
31	    return database.prepare('SELECT value FROM u_agent_team_operations').all()
32	      .map(row => JSON.parse((row as { value: string }).value) as Operation)
33	      .sort((left, right) => left.sequence - right.sequence)
34	  } finally {
35	    database.close()
36	  }
37	}
38	
39	function touchedThreadRefs(operation: Operation): readonly string[] {
40	  const data = operation.data ?? {}
41	  switch (operation.kind) {
42	    case 'team/message-sent':
43	    case 'team/thread-replied':
44	      return data.message?.threadRef === undefined ? [] : [data.message.threadRef]
45	    case 'team/thread-started':
46	      return data.anchor?.threadRef === undefined ? [] : [data.anchor.threadRef]
47	    case 'team/thread-promoted':
48	    case 'team/claim-created':
49	    case 'team/claim-done':
50	    case 'team/claim-released':
51	    case 'team/task-changed':
52	    case 'team/task-accountable-changed':
53	    case 'team/thread-attention-changed':
54	      return data.thread?.threadRef === undefined ? [] : [data.thread.threadRef]
55	    default:
56	      return []
57	  }
58	}
59	
60	function inboxMemberIds(inbox: Record<string, any> | undefined): Set<string> {
61	  const result = new Set<string>()
62	  if (inbox === undefined) return result
63	  for (const row of inbox.attention?.set ?? []) result.add(row.memberId)
64	  for (const row of inbox.attention?.removed ?? []) result.add(row.memberId)
65	  for (const field of ['directMarkers', 'activityMarkers', 'mainMarkers', 'reminderMarkers']) {
66	    for (const row of inbox[field]?.added ?? []) result.add(row.memberId)
67	    for (const row of inbox[field]?.removed ?? []) result.add(row.memberId)
68	  }
69	  return result
70	}
71	
72	function applyAttention(inbox: Record<string, any> | undefined, attention: Map<string, Set<string>>): void {
73	  for (const row of inbox?.attention?.removed ?? []) attention.get(row.threadRef)?.delete(row.memberId)
74	  for (const row of inbox?.attention?.set ?? []) {
75	    const followers = attention.get(row.threadRef) ?? new Set<string>()
76	    followers.add(row.memberId)
77	    attention.set(row.threadRef, followers)
78	  }
79	}
80	
81	function quantile(values: readonly number[], fraction: number): number | null {
82	  if (values.length === 0) return null
83	  const sorted = [...values].sort((left, right) => left - right)
84	  const position = (sorted.length - 1) * fraction
85	  const lower = Math.floor(position)
86	  const upper = Math.ceil(position)
87	  return lower === upper ? sorted[lower]! : sorted[lower]! + (sorted[upper]! - sorted[lower]!) * (position - lower)
88	}
89	
90	function distribution(values: readonly number[]) {
91	  return {
92	    count: values.length,
93	    p50: quantile(values, 0.5),
94	    p95: quantile(values, 0.95),
95	    p99: quantile(values, 0.99),
96	    max: values.length === 0 ? null : Math.max(...values),
97	    atLeast2: values.filter(value => value >= 2).length,
98	    atLeast4: values.filter(value => value >= 4).length,
99	    atLeast8: values.filter(value => value >= QUEUE_THRESHOLD).length,
100	  }
101	}
102	
103	function percent(part: number, total: number): number | null {
104	  return total === 0 ? null : Math.round(part / total * 10000) / 100
105	}
106	
107	const operations = readOperations(databasePath)
108	const members = new Map<string, Member>()
109	const attention = new Map<string, Set<string>>()
110	const operationKinds = new Map<string, number>()
111	const affectedRows: Array<{ readonly sequence: number; readonly occurredAt: string; readonly kind: string; readonly count: number }> = []
112	const replyRows: Array<{ readonly sequence: number; readonly occurredAt: string; readonly count: number }> = []
113	const threadWriteKinds = new Set([
114	  'team/message-sent', 'team/thread-replied', 'team/thread-started', 'team/thread-promoted',
115	  'team/claim-created', 'team/claim-done', 'team/claim-released', 'team/task-changed',
116	  'team/task-accountable-changed', 'team/thread-attention-changed',
117	])
118	
119	for (const operation of operations) {
120	  operationKinds.set(operation.kind, (operationKinds.get(operation.kind) ?? 0) + 1)
121	  const data = operation.data ?? {}
122	  if (operation.kind === 'team/member-added' && data.member?.memberId !== undefined) members.set(data.member.memberId, data.member)
123	  if (operation.kind === 'team/member-updated' && data.member?.memberId !== undefined) members.set(data.member.memberId, data.member)
124	  if (operation.kind === 'team/member-archived' || operation.kind === 'team/member-suspended') {
125	    const member = data.member
126	    if (member?.memberId !== undefined) members.set(member.memberId, member)
127	  }
128	  if (operation.kind === 'team/member-removed') members.delete(data.memberId)
129	
130	  applyAttention(data.inbox, attention)
131	  if (!threadWriteKinds.has(operation.kind)) continue
132	
133	  const affected = inboxMemberIds(data.inbox)
134	  for (const threadRef of touchedThreadRefs(operation)) {
135	    for (const memberId of attention.get(threadRef) ?? []) affected.add(memberId)
136	  }
137	  if (operation.actor?.kind === 'member' && operation.actor.memberId !== undefined) affected.add(operation.actor.memberId)
138	  const row = { sequence: operation.sequence, occurredAt: operation.occurredAt, kind: operation.kind, count: affected.size }
139	  affectedRows.push(row)
140	  if (operation.kind === 'team/thread-replied') replyRows.push({ sequence: row.sequence, occurredAt: row.occurredAt, count: row.count })
141	}
142	
143	const lastOccurredAt = operations.at(-1)?.occurredAt
144	const recentCutoff = lastOccurredAt === undefined ? 0 : Date.parse(lastOccurredAt) - 30 * DAY_MS
145	const recent = (rows: readonly { readonly occurredAt: string }[]) => rows.filter(row => Date.parse(row.occurredAt) >= recentCutoff)
146	const currentMembers = [...members.values()].filter(member => member.state !== 'archived').length
147	const enabledMemberIds = new Set([...members.values()].filter(member => member.state === undefined || member.state === 'enabled').map(member => member.memberId))
148	const memberStates = Object.fromEntries([...members.values()].reduce((counts, member) => {
149	  const state = member.state ?? 'unknown'
150	  counts.set(state, (counts.get(state) ?? 0) + 1)
151	  return counts
152	}, new Map<string, number>()))
153	const allFollowerCounts = [...attention.values()].map(followers => followers.size)
154	const enabledFollowerCounts = [...attention.values()].map(followers => [...followers].filter(memberId => enabledMemberIds.has(memberId)).length)
155	const thresholdRows = affectedRows.filter(row => row.count >= QUEUE_THRESHOLD)
156	const recentThresholdRows = recent(thresholdRows)
157	const thresholdByKind = Object.fromEntries([...new Set(thresholdRows.map(row => row.kind))].sort()
158	  .map(kind => [kind, thresholdRows.filter(row => row.kind === kind).length]))
159	const report = {
160	  databasePath,
161	  operationRange: operations.length === 0 ? null : { firstSequence: operations[0]!.sequence, lastSequence: operations.at(-1)!.sequence, firstOccurredAt: operations[0]!.occurredAt, lastOccurredAt },
162	  operationCount: operations.length,
163	  operationKinds: Object.fromEntries([...operationKinds].sort(([left], [right]) => left.localeCompare(right))),
164	  members: { current: currentMembers, enabled: enabledMemberIds.size, byState: memberStates },
165	  attention: {
166	    threadCount: attention.size,
167	    allMembers: distribution(allFollowerCounts),
168	    enabledMembers: distribution(enabledFollowerCounts),
169	  },
170	  affectedMemberEstimate: {
171	    threshold: QUEUE_THRESHOLD,
172	    allThreadWrites: distribution(affectedRows.map(row => row.count)),
173	    recent30dThreadWrites: distribution(recent(affectedRows).map(row => row.count)),
174	    thresholdHits: thresholdRows.length,
175	    thresholdHitPercent: percent(thresholdRows.length, affectedRows.length),
176	    recent30dThresholdHits: recentThresholdRows.length,
177	    recent30dThresholdHitPercent: percent(recentThresholdRows.length, recent(affectedRows).length),
178	    thresholdByKind,
179	  },
180	  replies: {
181	    all: distribution(replyRows.map(row => row.count)),
182	    recent30d: distribution(recent(replyRows).map(row => row.count)),
183	  },
184	  limitations: [
185	    'This report reads raw operations and Inbox deltas without current AgentTeamLedger replay, so legacy operation kinds remain measurable.',
186	    'Affected Member counts are conservative estimates from stored Inbox recipients, current Thread Attention after each operation, and the actor; Main stream recipient derivation is not included.',
187	    'The report contains counts only and never reads or prints Message bodies, handles, or operation request payloads.',
188	  ],
189	}
190	
191	if (jsonOutput) console.log(JSON.stringify(report, null, 2))
192	else {
193	  console.log(`ledger copy: ${databasePath}`)
194	  console.log(`operations: ${report.operationCount} (${report.operationRange?.firstOccurredAt ?? 'n/a'} – ${report.operationRange?.lastOccurredAt ?? 'n/a'})`)
195	  console.log(`members: ${report.members.current} current, ${report.members.enabled} enabled; Attention threads: ${report.attention.threadCount}`)
196	  console.log(`enabled follower count: p50 ${report.attention.enabledMembers.p50 ?? 'n/a'}, p95 ${report.attention.enabledMembers.p95 ?? 'n/a'}, max ${report.attention.enabledMembers.max ?? 'n/a'}; all durable Attention rows max ${report.attention.allMembers.max ?? 'n/a'}`)
197	  console.log(`thread-write affected estimate: p50 ${report.affectedMemberEstimate.allThreadWrites.p50 ?? 'n/a'}, p95 ${report.affectedMemberEstimate.allThreadWrites.p95 ?? 'n/a'}, max ${report.affectedMemberEstimate.allThreadWrites.max ?? 'n/a'}`)
198	  console.log(`queue threshold ${QUEUE_THRESHOLD}: ${report.affectedMemberEstimate.thresholdHits}/${report.affectedMemberEstimate.allThreadWrites.count} (${report.affectedMemberEstimate.thresholdHitPercent ?? 'n/a'}%); recent 30d ${report.affectedMemberEstimate.recent30dThresholdHits}/${report.affectedMemberEstimate.recent30dThreadWrites.count} (${report.affectedMemberEstimate.recent30dThresholdHitPercent ?? 'n/a'}%)`)
199	  console.log(`reply affected estimate: all p95 ${report.replies.all.p95 ?? 'n/a'}, max ${report.replies.all.max ?? 'n/a'}; recent 30d p95 ${report.replies.recent30d.p95 ?? 'n/a'}, max ${report.replies.recent30d.max ?? 'n/a'}`)
200	}

1	# Team performance evaluation
2	
3	English | [中文](team-performance.zh.md)
4	
5	## Purpose
6	
7	The Team performance suite measures the costs that a human or Member can observe across loading, tool calls, ledger reads, Session work, and collaboration. It is an evaluation tool, not a production code path, and it runs only when explicitly enabled.
8	
9	The source of the scenarios is [`scripts/team-performance/`](../../scripts/team-performance/). The script index lists the entry points and their output formats in [`scripts/README.md`](../../scripts/README.md).
10	
11	## Run the evaluation
12	
13	### Baseline
14	
15	Run the default 16 scenarios in one Node process:
16	
17	```sh
18	DSH_BENCH_TEAM=1 npm run bench:team
19	```
20	
21	The command writes a run directory under `artifacts/team-perf/runs/` containing `manifest.json`, measured `samples.jsonl`, and `summary.json`. The default configuration uses three measured samples and one warmup. Use `DSH_BENCH_SCENARIOS` to select scenarios and the matching variables such as `DSH_BENCH_THREADS`, `DSH_BENCH_FOLLOWERS`, `DSH_BENCH_MEMBERS`, and `DSH_BENCH_SESSION_EVENTS` to change workload size.
22	
23	### Scale matrix
24	
25	Run the default 15 cases in separate Node processes:
26	
27	```sh
28	npm run bench:team:matrix
29	```
30	
31	Set `DSH_BENCH_MATRIX_CASES` to a comma-separated list of `scenario:threads:followers`. The default collaboration cases cover the observed 1–4 follower range, the eight-Member queue boundary, a 20-Thread backlog, and one 32-follower stress case. The matrix routes the first size to Member or Session workloads when the scenario requires it. Each matrix directory contains a manifest, each child run, and an aggregated `results.json`.
32	
33	### Real profile usage
34	
35	Summarize an explicit read-only SQLite copy from a real profile:
36	
37	```sh
38	npm run bench:team:usage -- /path/to/agent_team.sqlite --json
39	```
40	
41	The report counts operations, Members, Thread Attention sizes, reply impact, and operations near the notification queue threshold. It reads raw operations instead of forcing the current ledger replay, so old `team/channel-*` records remain measurable.
42	
43	Affected Member counts are estimates: they include stored Inbox recipients, Thread Attention after each operation, and the actor, but omit Main stream recipient derivation. The report prints counts only and never prints Message bodies or handles.
44	
45	### Browser loading
46	
47	Measure the assembled Web bundle and Team mode:
48	
49	```sh
50	DSH_BENCH_BROWSER_SAMPLES=3 npm run bench:team:browser
51	```
52	
53	Each sample uses a fresh temporary Web scaffold and Chromium. The runner records page load, Workspace connection, ordinary ready, Team mode ready, navigation timing, transfer bytes, console warnings, and page errors. It writes `manifest.json`, `samples.jsonl`, and `summary.json` under `artifacts/team-perf/browser/runs/`. Browser results must be read with p95 and p99 and with the individual samples because cold startup variance is material.
54	
55	### Semantic probes
56	
57	Check the ordered post-commit notification queue:
58	
59	```sh
60	DSH_BENCH_TEAM=1 npm run bench:team:semantics
61	```
62	
63	The probe checks failed delivery retry, per-Member ordering, Client invalidation before notification drain, shutdown cancellation, and disposal errors. A passing timing run does not replace these checks.
64	
65	### Compare runs
66	
67	Compare two baseline summaries or two matrix result files:
68	
69	```sh
70	npm run bench:team:compare -- before/summary.json after/summary.json
71	npm run bench:team:compare -- --max-regression 20 before/summary.json after/summary.json
72	```
73	
74	The comparator reports shared p50, p95, and p99 rows and separately reports missing scenarios, missing metrics, and invalid measurements. With `--max-regression`, a metric with no measured percentiles fails the comparison; a zero-to-positive baseline change also fails instead of being treated as incomparable. A regression threshold is meaningful only when the workload, environment, and scenario schema match.
75	
76	## What the scenarios measure
77	
78	| Area | Scenarios | Main evidence |
79	| --- | --- | --- |
80	| Loading and activation | `bundle-size`, `host-boot`, `member-activation`, `member-activation-batch`, `member-resume` | bundle bytes, Host fixture boot, new and resumed Member activation, sequential versus concurrent activation |
81	| Tool paths | `tool-call`, `tool-read-sweep`, `thread-read-reply`, `tool-write`, `notification-retry` | tool total, Host handler time, result bytes, read/reply and failed-delivery recovery |
82	| Collaboration | `collaboration-fanout`, `collaboration-agent-turn` | durable commit, Ledger queue wait/service, fan-out dispatch, event-loop lag, notification drain, model request and idle stages |
83	| Session and storage | `session-fold`, `session-replay-jsonl`, `ledger-read-memory`, `ledger-replay-sqlite` | cursor and projection fold, JSONL write/read/bytes, bounded ledger reads, SQLite open/replay/validation |
84	
85	The baseline uses real Team Host fixtures and deterministic model adapters where a model turn is needed. It does not claim to represent a production model provider or a live user's machine. The browser scenario is the assembled-path check; the Node scenarios explain the cost inside that path.
86	
87	## Current constraints
88	
89	- Notification read material is reused only during one delivery attempt. Facts, delivery plans, and projections are not long-lived caches or a second authority.
90	- A commit affecting at least eight Members queues notification effects after the durable commit and Client invalidation. Effects remain ordered per Member and are scheduled independently across Members. Effects that have not started when shutdown begins are skipped; the next activation derives the durable unread facts again.
91	- JSONL `zstd` remains the production default. Uncompressed replay is faster in the measured fixture but uses substantially more disk space.
92	- Concurrent calls already improve the measured batch Member activation path. The result alone does not justify changing Host startup ordering without a separate startup-restoration experiment.
93	- Browser cold-start results have a long tail. Keep the sample records and compare distributions; do not turn one run into a hard acceptance threshold.
94	
95	## Change workflow
96	
97	When changing a performance-sensitive path, run the narrowest scenario that can observe the change, then run the related scale cases and semantic probes. Compare the same scenario before and after the change. Inspect operation counts and result shape together with wall-clock values; a lower time with missing facts is a failed run. Run `npm test` and `npm run check:artifact` before treating the result as delivered.
98	
99	Do not place secrets, real profiles, or temporary browser overlays in the repository. The benchmark is opt-in, so ordinary development and release checks do not run it.
100

3	**What to build:** 一次通知投递只派生一次该 Member 的 Thread/Main unread 材料和 delivery plan，文本渲染、identity、coverage 和投递复用同一份只读结果，同时保持当前通知内容、顺序、attempt 和失败语义。
4	**Blocked by:** 01
5	**Status:** four safe slices implemented; failure/generation semantic coverage remains open
6	
7	- [x] `deliverInboxNotice` 复用本次已经生成的 delivery plan，去掉 `notificationText` 的重复 plan 计算
8	- [x] `notificationFacts` 在一次同步读取中复用 `memberInbox` 已派生的 unread facts；返回结构和 durable authority 不变
9	- [x] `running` 状态边沿在已有完整 notice coverage 时跳过重复读取；失败后的空 coverage 仍然进入重试路径
10	- [x] Thread/Main unread、delivery plan 和文本渲染不再对同一投递重复扫描同一批 facts
11	- [x] 1/20/100 unread Thread 和 1/8/32 follower 的矩阵调用计数已记录；per-member fan-out 仍是 O(follower × unread Thread) 候选
12	- [ ] notice text、covered、undelivered、attempt 和 steer/followup 顺序与旧路径逐项一致
13	- [ ] wake、recovery、generation swap、通知派生失败和 steer 失败的行为保持现有隔离语义
14	- [ ] 相关 Host、ledger、delivery 和 tool 回归通过

17	
18	当前只做短生命周期 read set 和一个 lifecycle edge 的快速返回：`notificationText` 接收当前 delivery plan，`notificationFacts` 在一次调用内复用 `memberInbox` 的 unread facts，`notificationSnapshot` 让 Thread/Main unread 在一次通知投递内共享 `memberInbox` 已算出的结果，`running` 只在已有非空 coverage 时跳过。没有把 facts、plan 或 projection 放入长期缓存，也没有改变 ledger 的读取接口。32 follower 样本确认每个受影响 Member 的 facts、plan 和文本派生保持一次，`mainUnreadFrom` 从 66 次降为 33 次；达到 fan-out 阈值后，通知 effect 在 durable commit 和 Client invalidation 后进入按 Member 保序的队列，关闭开始后未执行的通知取消并由下次 activation 重派。失败重试、关闭取消、顺序和 Client invalidation 的语义探针均通过。

1	import { access, mkdtemp, readdir, readFile, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
2	import { constants } from 'node:fs'
3	import { dirname, join, resolve } from 'node:path'
4	import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
5	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
6	import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
7	import { harnessDir } from './harness-dir.mjs'
8	
9	const root = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..')
10	const harness = harnessDir
11	const chrome = process.env.CHROME_PATH ?? '/usr/bin/google-chrome'
12	const temporary = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'dsh-agent-team-browser-'))
13	const home = join(temporary, 'home')
14	// Every scenario is its own file under scripts/e2e/, so the runner renders and
15	// runs each one inside the harness checkout. Keeping them separate means one
16	// slow journey cannot widen another's budget, and a failure names its file.
17	// `support.ts` rides along as a sibling, because the rendered files import it
18	// relatively — exactly where the one monolithic script used to sit.
19	const sourceDir = join(root, 'scripts', 'e2e')
20	const scenarios = (await readdir(sourceDir)).filter(name => name.endsWith('.e2e.ts') || name === 'support.ts').sort()
21	
22	const quote = value => value.replaceAll('\\', '\\\\').replaceAll("'", "\\'")
23	
24	const run = (command, args, cwd) => new Promise((resolveRun, reject) => {
25	  // Windows: bare-name pnpm shim spawns fail (.cmd ENOENT, and Node 22+ refuses shell-less .cmd spawns), so go through cmd.exe with the argument string quoted.
26	  const child = process.platform === 'win32'
27	    ? spawn(`${command} ${args.join(' ')}`, { cwd, stdio: 'inherit', env: process.env, shell: true })
28	    : spawn(command, args, { cwd, stdio: 'inherit', env: process.env })
29	  child.once('error', reject)
30	  child.once('exit', code => code === 0 ? resolveRun() : reject(new Error(`${command} exited with ${code}`)))
31	})
32	
33	/** The staged copy every scenario runs against; the alphabetically-first scenario creates it, and the rest reuse it. */
34	const staged = join(home, 'profiles', 'node_modules', '@contexera', 'dsh-agent-team')
35	const rendered = []
36	try {
37	  await access(join(harness, 'apps/web/dist/index.html'), constants.R_OK)
38	  await access(chrome, constants.X_OK)
39	  for (const scenario of scenarios) {
40	    const template = await readFile(join(sourceDir, scenario), 'utf8')
41	    const target = join(harness, 'apps/web', 'tests', scenario === 'support.ts' ? '__external-agent-team-support.ts' : `__external-agent-team-${scenario}`)
42	    await writeFile(target, template
43	      .replaceAll('__TEAM_ROOT__', quote(root))
44	      .replaceAll('__HOME__', quote(home))
45	      .replaceAll('__CHROME__', quote(chrome)))
46	    // Every rendered file is removed again, support included: a leftover in the
47	    // Harness checkout is a stray untracked file in a repository this bundle
48	    // must not modify.
49	    rendered.push(target)
50	  }
51	  await run('corepack', ['pnpm', 'exec', 'vitest', 'run', '--config', 'vitest.web.config.ts',
52	    ...rendered.filter(path => path.endsWith('.e2e.ts')).map(path => path.slice(harness.length + 1).replaceAll('\\', '/')),
53	    '--reporter=verbose', ...process.argv.slice(2)], harness)
54	} finally {
55	  await Promise.all(rendered.map(path => rm(path, { force: true })))
56	  await rm(temporary, { recursive: true, force: true })
57	}

1	import { access, mkdtemp, readdir, readFile, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
2	import { constants } from 'node:fs'
3	import { dirname, join, resolve } from 'node:path'
4	import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
5	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
6	import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
7	import { harnessDir } from './harness-dir.mjs'
8	
9	const root = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..')
10	const harness = harnessDir
11	const chrome = process.env.CHROME_PATH ?? '/usr/bin/google-chrome'
12	const temporary = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'dsh-agent-team-browser-'))
13	const home = join(temporary, 'home')
14	// Every scenario is its own file under scripts/e2e/, so the runner renders and
15	// runs each one inside the harness checkout. Keeping them separate means one
16	// slow journey cannot widen another's budget, and a failure names its file.
17	// `support.ts` rides along as a sibling, because the rendered files import it
18	// relatively — exactly where the one monolithic script used to sit.
19	const sourceDir = join(root, 'scripts', 'e2e')
20	const scenarios = (await readdir(sourceDir)).filter(name => name.endsWith('.e2e.ts') || name === 'support.ts').sort()
21	
22	const quote = value => value.replaceAll('\\', '\\\\').replaceAll("'", "\\'")
23	
24	const run = (command, args, cwd) => new Promise((resolveRun, reject) => {
25	  // Windows: bare-name pnpm shim spawns fail (.cmd ENOENT, and Node 22+ refuses shell-less .cmd spawns), so go through cmd.exe with the argument string quoted.
26	  const child = process.platform === 'win32'
27	    ? spawn(`${command} ${args.join(' ')}`, { cwd, stdio: 'inherit', env: process.env, shell: true })
28	    : spawn(command, args, { cwd, stdio: 'inherit', env: process.env })
29	  child.once('error', reject)
30	  child.once('exit', code => code === 0 ? resolveRun() : reject(new Error(`${command} exited with ${code}`)))
31	})
32	
33	/** The staged copy every scenario runs against; the alphabetically-first scenario creates it, and the rest reuse it. */
34	const staged = join(home, 'profiles', 'node_modules', '@contexera', 'dsh-agent-team')
35	const rendered = []
36	try {
37	  await access(join(harness, 'apps/web/dist/index.html'), constants.R_OK)
38	  await access(chrome, constants.X_OK)
39	  for (const scenario of scenarios) {
40	    const template = await readFile(join(sourceDir, scenario), 'utf8')
41	    const target = join(harness, 'apps/web', 'tests', scenario === 'support.ts' ? '__external-agent-team-support.ts' : `__external-agent-team-${scenario}`)
42	    await writeFile(target, template
43	      .replaceAll('__TEAM_ROOT__', quote(root))
44	      .replaceAll('__HOME__', quote(home))
45	      .replaceAll('__CHROME__', quote(chrome)))
46	    // Every rendered file is removed again, support included: a leftover in the
47	    // Harness checkout is a stray untracked file in a repository this bundle
48	    // must not modify.
49	    rendered.push(target)
50	  }
51	  await run('corepack', ['pnpm', 'exec', 'vitest', 'run', '--config', 'vitest.web.config.ts',
52	    ...rendered.filter(path => path.endsWith('.e2e.ts')).map(path => path.slice(harness.length + 1).replaceAll('\\', '/')),
53	    '--reporter=verbose', ...process.argv.slice(2)], harness)
54	} finally {
55	  await Promise.all(rendered.map(path => rm(path, { force: true })))
56	  await rm(temporary, { recursive: true, force: true })
57	}

1	/**
2	 * Shared boot helpers for the Host ledger specs.
3	 *
4	 * Every spec in this directory boots the real `AgentTeam` plugin over a
5	 * throwaway storage domain, so the two builders here are the one copy of that
6	 * arrangement: a spec picks the backend it needs and describes behavior. They
7	 * are deliberately not a fixture registry — a spec that needs a different
8	 * arrangement builds it locally and keeps it local.
9	 */
10	import { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
11	import Storage from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage'
12	import { DomainFacility } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-domain'
13	import type { KvTable } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-domain'
14	import SessionProjectionRegistry from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-projection'
15	import { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
16	import { WorkspaceId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace'
17	import { MemoryMediaPool, MemoryStorageBackend } from './memory-backend.ts'
18	import { provideQuietTokenMeter } from './team-host-fixture.ts'
19	import { SqliteStorageBackend } from '../../src/vendor/storage-sqlite/index.ts'
20	import AgentTeam from '../../src/index.ts'
21	import { agentTeamDomainSpec } from '../../src/spec.ts'
22	import { AgentTeamLedger, agentTeamHumanActor } from '../../src/ledger.ts'
23	import type { AgentTeamAgentMember, AgentTeamMemberActor, AgentTeamOperation, AgentTeamOperationId, AgentTeamRequestId, AgentTeamTask } from '../../src/types.ts'
24	
25	export interface TeamHarness {
26	  readonly ctx: Context
27	  readonly fiber: Awaited<ReturnType<Context['plugin']>>
28	  readonly facility: DomainFacility
29	}
30	
31	export interface SqliteTeamHarness extends TeamHarness {
32	  readonly backend: SqliteStorageBackend
33	}
34	
35	/** The two Workspaces the Host specs address; a third is built locally where a spec needs one. */
36	export const alpha = WorkspaceId('workspace:alpha')
37	export const beta = WorkspaceId('workspace:beta')
38	
39	/** One stable request id per logical write, so a replay asserts the same id. */
40	export const requestId = (value: string): AgentTeamRequestId => value as AgentTeamRequestId
41	
42	/** Boot the Team over a memory pool: the default for anything that does not survive a restart. */
43	export async function harness(
44	  pool = new MemoryMediaPool(),
45	  workspaceIds = [alpha],
46	  config?: { readonly gate?: { readonly tokens?: number; readonly idleMs?: number; readonly judgeTimeoutMs?: number } },
47	): Promise<TeamHarness> {
48	  const ctx = new Context()
49	  await ctx.plugin(Storage)
50	  ctx.storage.backend.register('memory', new MemoryStorageBackend(pool))
51	  const facility = new DomainFacility(ctx, { backend: 'memory', routes: {} })
52	  ctx.storage.mount('domain', facility)
53	  ctx.provide('storageDomain', facility)
54	  ctx.provide('workspaceRegistry', {
55	    get: (id: WorkspaceId) => workspaceIds.includes(id) ? { id, path: process.cwd(), attachSession: async () => {} } : undefined,
56	    list: () => workspaceIds.map(id => ({ id, path: process.cwd() })),
57	    archiveSession: async () => {},
58	  })
59	  ctx.provide('agents', { create: async () => { throw new Error('unused') }, resume: async () => { throw new Error('unused') } })
60	  ctx.provide('agentDefaultModel', { currentSelection: () => ({ provider: 'mock', model: 'mock' }) })
61	  ctx.provide('agentPresets', { mount: async () => { throw new Error('unused') } })
62	  ctx.provide('tools', { schemas: () => [] })
63	  ctx.provide('sessionPersistence', { list: async () => [] })
64	  provideQuietTokenMeter(ctx)
65	  await ctx.plugin(SessionProjectionRegistry)
66	  const fiber = config === undefined ? await ctx.plugin(AgentTeam) : await ctx.plugin(AgentTeam, config)
67	  return { ctx, fiber, facility }
68	}
69	
70	/** Boot the Team over a SQLite file: the shape that survives a dispose and a reopen. */
71	export async function sqliteHarness(path: string): Promise<SqliteTeamHarness> {
72	  const ctx = new Context()
73	  await ctx.plugin(Storage)
74	  const backend = new SqliteStorageBackend({ path, journalMode: 'delete' })
75	  ctx.storage.backend.register('sqlite', backend)
76	  const facility = new DomainFacility(ctx, { backend: 'sqlite', routes: {} })
77	  ctx.storage.mount('domain', facility)
78	  ctx.provide('storageDomain', facility)
79	  ctx.provide('workspaceRegistry', { get: (id: WorkspaceId) => ({ id, path: process.cwd(), attachSession: async () => {}, archiveSession: async () => {} }), list: () => [] })
80	  ctx.provide('agents', { create: async () => { throw new Error('unused') }, resume: async () => { throw new Error('unused') } })
81	  ctx.provide('agentDefaultModel', { currentSelection: () => ({ provider: 'mock', model: 'mock' }) })
82	  ctx.provide('agentPresets', { mount: async () => { throw new Error('unused') } })
83	  ctx.provide('tools', { schemas: () => [] })
84	  ctx.provide('sessionPersistence', { list: async () => [] })
85	  provideQuietTokenMeter(ctx)
86	  await ctx.plugin(SessionProjectionRegistry)
87	  const fiber = await ctx.plugin(AgentTeam)
88	  return { ctx, fiber, facility, backend }
89	}
90	
91	/**
92	 * The ledger a cold boot builds over the table a harness already wrote. The
93	 * handle is reached through the facility rather than cached, so a reopened
94	 * harness is read through its own domain instance.
95	 */
96	export function ledgerAtBoot(test: TeamHarness): AgentTeamLedger {
97	  return new AgentTeamLedger(test.facility.get('agent_team')!.table('operations') as unknown as KvTable<AgentTeamOperationId, AgentTeamOperation>)
98	}
99	
100	/** One enabled Agent Member in one Workspace, plus the actor that speaks as it. */
101	export async function addLedgerMember(
102	  ledger: AgentTeamLedger,
103	  projectRef: string | undefined,
104	  memberId = `member:agent-${crypto.randomUUID()}`,
105	  description = 'Test Agent',
106	  handle = memberId.slice('member:'.length),
107	): Promise<{ readonly member: AgentTeamAgentMember; readonly actor: AgentTeamMemberActor }> {
108	  const member: AgentTeamAgentMember = {
109	    memberId: memberId as never,
110	    sessionId: SessionId(`session:${memberId}`),
111	    workspaceId: alpha,
112	    handle,
113	    description,
114	    presetId: 'team-member',
115	    privateMemoryPath: `/tmp/${memberId}`,
116	    state: 'enabled',
117	  }
118	  await ledger.addMember({ requestId: requestId(`add:${memberId}`), actor: agentTeamHumanActor(), member, handle: member.handle,
119	    description: member.description, presetId: member.presetId, workspaceId: alpha,
120	    projectRefs: projectRef === undefined ? [] : [projectRef as never] })
121	  return { member, actor: { kind: 'member', memberId: member.memberId, handle: member.handle } }
122	}
123	
124	/** Starting a Thread is a Project owner's act; the Human grants the standing. */
125	export const makeOwner = (ledger: AgentTeamLedger, projectRef: string, memberId: string, workspaceId: WorkspaceId = alpha) =>
126	  ledger.addProjectOwner({ requestId: requestId(`owner:${workspaceId}:${projectRef}:${memberId}`), actor: agentTeamHumanActor(),
127	    workspaceId, projectRef: projectRef as never, memberId: memberId as never })
128	
129	/** The in-progress and in-review rows of a Member's Task board, shaped like the address-book radar the board replaced. */
130	export function inFlight(ledger: AgentTeamLedger, workspaceId: WorkspaceId, memberId: AgentTeamAgentMember['memberId']) {
131	  const actor = { kind: 'member' as const, memberId, handle: ledger.getMember(memberId)!.handle }
132	  return ledger.taskBoard(actor, { workspaceId }).open.filter(item => item.task.status === 'in_progress' || item.task.status === 'in_review')
133	    .map(item => ({ threadRef: item.threadRef, taskRef: item.task.taskRef, status: item.task.status, subject: item.subject, taskNumber: item.taskNumber, members: item.liveClaimOwners }))
134	}
135	
136	/** Narrow one result to its committed variant, naming the kind that refused it. */
137	export function committed<T extends { readonly kind: string }>(result: T): Extract<T, { readonly kind: 'committed' }> {
138	  if (result.kind !== 'committed') throw new Error(`expected committed result, received ${result.kind}`)
139	  return result as Extract<T, { readonly kind: 'committed' }>
140	}
141	
142	/** Narrow one result to the shape that carries a Task. */
143	export function withTask<T extends { readonly task?: AgentTeamTask }>(result: T): T & { readonly task: AgentTeamTask } {
144	  if (result.task === undefined) throw new Error('expected Task overlay')
145	  return result as T & { readonly task: AgentTeamTask }
146	}

148	/** A memory pool already holding one stored operations table, for replay-only specs. */
149	export function storedPool(records: Array<[string, unknown]>, version: number = agentTeamDomainSpec.version): MemoryMediaPool {
150	  const pool = new MemoryMediaPool()
151	  pool.versions.set('agent_team', version)
152	  pool.media.set('agent_team', { tables: new Map([['operations', new Map(records)]]), global: null })
153	  return pool
154	}

本轮评测资产已经足够支持加载、tool call、ledger、Session 和协作路径的持续对照；下一步不再增加新的 fan-out 调度层。生产侧保留 read-set、delivery plan 复用、running coverage 跳过和低频有序通知队列；评测侧保留一个 32 follower 压力档，用于防止极端协作回归。

# Review 02 — 修复复核与新增使用统计审查

**Conclusion:** Changes needed
**Work item:** `.scratch/active/team-performance-optimization`
**Ticket:** Whole work item（01–03）
**Compared:** HEAD `f4de5a01c0edb8626a4d6ada5b6d2cc1ba4a5c1f` 上的未提交性能改动，包括全部未跟踪的 `scripts/team-performance/` 和性能文档
**Commits:** 本轮未创建提交
**Reviewed:** 2026-10-30 19:08–19:20 UTC+8

## Findings

### P2 — 恢复后的 Member 仍被使用统计报告为 suspended

**Location:** `scripts/team-performance/team-live-usage.ts:119–128,146–154`。

**Evidence:** 新脚本依次处理 `member-added`、`member-updated`、`member-archived`、`member-suspended`、`member-removed`，遗漏 `team/member-resumed`。而该操作在 `packages/agent-team/src/types/operations.ts:63–65` 明确携带恢复后的完整 Member。

本轮用真实 `sqliteHarness` 和 `AgentTeamLedger` 创建临时 SQLite，依次执行 `addMember → suspendMember → resumeMember`。关闭写入端后，通过 `team-live-usage.ts <database> --json` 读取。未接触用户真实 profile。

```json
{
  "expected": { "memberState": "enabled", "enabled": 1, "suspended": 0 },
  "actual": { "current": 1, "enabled": 0, "byState": { "suspended": 1 } },
  "operations": {
    "team/initialized": 1,
    "team/member-added": 1,
    "team/member-resumed": 1,
    "team/member-suspended": 1,
    "team/rules-version-adopted": 1
  }
}
```

**Impact:** 有过暂停和恢复、之后没有其他覆盖 Member 快照的操作时，脚本低估 enabled Member 数，并把其 Thread Attention 从 `enabledMembers` 统计中排除。新文档和工作项使用该统计描述日常协作规模，因此相关数字需要修正后重新生成。这不证明当前真实 profile 的具体数字必然有误，但证明脚本不能可靠计算这类历史。

**Basis:** 新性能文档承诺统计真实 profile 的 Member 和 Thread Attention；ticket 01/03 要求测量结果与输入事实一致。源码与真实 ledger 的当前状态是事实依据。

**Suggested fix:** 把 `team/member-resumed` 纳入 Member 状态更新；增加添加、暂停、恢复、归档和移除序列的自动测试，并断言 enabled Member 及 enabled follower 计数。修复后重新生成用于工作项结论的真实 profile 统计。

## 上轮发现的复核

| 问题 | 结果 | 本轮证据 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 大批次后小批次插队 | 已修正 | `pendingNotification` 存在时继续排入同一 Member 链；语义探针观察到 8 个 sequence 12 后接 sequence 13 |
| 空测量和零基线误判为通过 | 已修正 | CLI 对照：10→10 退出 0；10→20、10→无样本、0→20 均退出 1 |
| 相对 Harness checkout 记录 unknown | 已修正 | `DSH_HARNESS_DIR=deepseek-harness` 实跑正确记录 `687f282e8625c6b8d11ff58211a90524be2e4317` |
| 延迟 invariant 与文档不一致 | 已修正 | Host authority 双语文档与注释均区分同步 reject 和异步 error 日志；相关测试通过 |
| Where to start 缺入口 | 已修正 | 两种语言均新增性能测量导航；`npm test` 中的 docs gate 通过 |

移除每次通知入队/完成时聚合全部链的 `notificationEffectTail`，评测改为观察 `notificationEffectTails`，未恢复新的长期事实缓存。该调整没有改变 ledger 权威。

## Acceptance criteria

| 条件 | 结果 | 证据 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 01.1–01.6 基准场景、采样、标识、产物与默认关闭 | 有实现，部分复跑 | 复跑 Host boot；脚本和文档包含其余场景，未重跑完整基线 |
| 01.7 比较器与回归门槛 | Met（本轮四组边界） | 正常、回归、空测量、零基线结果均符合预期 |
| 01.8 clean commit 矩阵 | Not verified | 本次修改仍未提交，不能把工作树样本记作 clean commit 证据 |
| 02.1–02.5 单次派生复用与 running 去重 | 保留实现，现有回归通过 | Ledger read set、plan 复用、undelivered 重试条件保持；Host/Inbox 25 测试通过 |
| 02.6 text/covered/undelivered/attempt 与旧路径逐项一致 | Partial | 混合批次顺序修复已验证；仍未提供完整旧新等价测试 |
| 02.7 recovery/generation/失败隔离 | Partial | 失败重试、shutdown、invariant 和 mixed-batch 探针通过；没有专项验证全部 generation 交错 |

| --- | --- |
| `git diff --check HEAD` | 退出 0 |
| `npx vitest run packages/agent-team/tests/post-commit-delivery.spec.ts packages/agent-team/tests/inbox-delivery.spec.ts` | 2 文件，25 测试通过 |
| `DSH_BENCH_TEAM=1 npm run bench:team:semantics` | 退出 0，五项通过；shutdown 后执行数 0，mixed-batch 保序 |
| `node artifacts/team-perf/review-2026-10-30/compare-check.mjs` | 四组 CLI 边界符合预期，详见上表 |
| `DSH_BENCH_TEAM=1 DSH_HARNESS_DIR=deepseek-harness DSH_BENCH_SAMPLES=1 DSH_BENCH_WARMUPS=0 DSH_BENCH_SCENARIOS=host-boot npm run bench:team` | 退出 0；Harness commit 正确 |
| `node --import tsx artifacts/team-perf/review-final-2026-10-30/usage-state.ts` | 退出 0，成功采集反例；报告 enabled 0，对照 ledger enabled 1。这是缺陷复现，不是行为通过 |
| `npm test` | 退出 0；135 文件通过，1 跳过；1540 测试通过，1 跳过；前置文档、边界等检查通过 |

| 受审源码审查前后 SHA-256 | 一致，无并发改写证据 |

## Unverified scope and residual risk

    {
      "id": "crystal_bc36bfd6df65",
      "title": "dsh-agent-team 审查—核验—修复—观察的闭环方法论：三条口径、三分法核验与基线指标收尾",
      "content": "[[dsh-agent-team]] 在 2026-10 连续跑了两轮「外部审查 → 逐条核验 → 修复落地 → 留观察」的闭环，两轮共同暴露出的不是零散 bug，而是一套**可复用的审查-修复方法论**：审查的价值取决于先立口径，修复的价值取决于是否保留可撤销的观察期。

## 一、审查前必须先立三条口径（否则必然产出伪缺陷）
以 ticket 06/07 的只读审查为例，开工前固定：
- **范围**：`packages/tool-agent-team`、`packages/client-agent-team`、`packages/agent-team/preset`、`core-skills` 及当次交付；依据 spec.md 指定章节与 issues。
- **行为以源码和测试为准，不以文档为准**；只读，不改代码。
- **两条禁令**：不得把**规划中**的功能（accountable/transfer/accept-close-reopen/sourceThreadRefs）当作已实现；不得把 spec 的**撤回项**当作实现偏差。没有这两条，审查会同时产生大量伪缺陷和噪声。

## 二、核验他人审查：三分法而不是二分法
对一份 15 条外部 review 逐条核实（master 4c72362）的结论分布是：**10 条成立 / 3 条部分成立 / 1 条不成立**。
- 「部分成立」是最有价值的一档：机制对而提示语不准（`self_acceptance_forbidden`）、文件存在只是被 `.scratch/active` ignore 挡在 git 外、文档确未更新但「中英不同步」查无实据（中英对在同提交成对更新）。
- 不成立的一条同样是资产：Client 侧「从已加载窗口推算看板」的回退早已在 07 删除，只剩 `boardEmpty` 文案残留——**核验要把「已修」与「仍未修」明确分开，否则旧结论会被反复重提**。
- 核验要顺手扩围：指出同类但未列出的位置（如 `index.ts:652` 的 body 描述与两处 docs 矛盾）。
- 量化证据优于形容词：`ledger.ts` 6099 行、`rulesVersion` 出现 41 处（严格版本分支 29 处），这类数字是「结构性问题」唯一可证伪的形式。

## 三、缺陷的根因模式（两轮反复出现）
- **规则版本既是行为开关又被当成历史解释器**：v1→v2 采纳后，对 v1 回复做 requestId 重放会用**当前**规则重算 recipients，导致同一回复重试得到不同收件人并抛 `throwRequestCollision`。两个角色必须分离。
- **读写两侧校验强度不对称**：写路径用 `requireProjectMemberActor`，读路径只校验 Workspace participation → 拿到 threadRef 的非成员可读、可 follow，而 follow 会写入成员派生，等于**自助取得 Project 成员身份**。所有读侧入口必须与写侧共用同一成员判定。
- **测试的覆盖形状决定缺陷能否存活**：owner 唤醒 fan-out 缺失之所以长期未被发现，是因为唯一相关测试用了 mention——正好绕开缺口。
- **「标记已读」与「纳入快照」必须同一次操作**：`markRead` 只保留 standing 而丢弃 entries，指向首页 20 条之前的 marker 被消费后，该消息永不进入快照，丢消息是静默的。
- **规则版本切换时，文案与注释必须在同一张 checklist 上**：否则代码对了、说明还在说旧话，下游 agent 会按旧文案推理（`@all` 在 v2 已退化为普通文本，文档仍在宣称它触达整个 Project）。
- **干净检出的隐形雷**：`packages/agent-team/node_modules/zod` 是被 git 跟踪的自指符号链接（内容是机器绝对路径），干净 clone 即损坏——审查必须验证「从零 clone 能否构建」。

## 四、修复后的处置纪律：分类修复 + 保留观察 + 指标兜底
四项修复落地（commit e29ed2c，未 push）的处置方式本身是范式：
- **A｜reopen 恢复 accountable follow**：新 reopen 用 `refollowedMembers` 判别，旧记录保持 marker-only、**不升规则版本**——修 bug 不应顺带触发规则迁移。
- **B｜提醒按当前 durable 条件过滤**：读取时过滤，不改写 marker、不重查 idle，避免修复引入新的写放大。
- **C｜Agent idle ≥30min 与 error 清 idle 保持原状，继续试用观察**——机制可疑但证据不足时，先观察而不是改。
- **D｜文档、升级说明、runbook、`boardEmpty`、recovery 文案、统计脚本一并完成**。

验证判据要真实：真实 SQLite 副本 24625 条重放通过、18 条旧 reopen 兼容、1285 测试与浏览器 8/8 通过。

## 五、闭环的最后一步：用基线指标替代印象
修复不是终点。spec §11 的试用节奏曾在 06–09 一起上线时被跳过，代价是**指标无法归因**。正确收尾：用在线备份出的新 SQLite 副本跑 `scripts/team-trial-metrics.ts`，对比上线前基线（11 条 Agent 回复 / 0 条 Agent 间、4 次 accept-close 全 Human、0 条非 owner 主对话发言、5 条提醒 / 0 条失效未读），并对 `staleUnreadSamples` 与已消费提醒人工判定误报；**绝不打开真实账本**。同时，08 的 Task accountability 工具侧（transfer、accept/close/reopen、`team_message.start` 的 accountable 与 sourceThreadRefs、按动作强制参数口袋）已实现并全量验证（tool-agent-team 87/87、vitest 1247 通过），核验时须把它视为「已落地」而非「规划中」。

**总判据**：审查要能分辨「规划中 / 已实现 / 已修」，修复要能分辨「必改 / 留着观察」，收尾要能分辨「感觉变好了」与「基线指标变了」。

      "title": "dsh-agent-team 审查—核验—修复—观察的闭环方法论：三条口径、三分法核验与基线指标收尾",
      "content": "[[dsh-agent-team]] 在 2026-10 连续跑了两轮「外部审查 → 逐条核验 → 修复落地 → 留观察」的闭环，两轮共同暴露出的不是零散 bug，而是一套**可复用的审查-修复方法论**：审查的价值取决于先立口径，修复的价值取决于是否保留可撤销的观察期。

## 一、审查前必须先立三条口径（否则必然产出伪缺陷）
以 ticket 06/07 的只读审查为例，开工前固定：
- **范围**：`packages/tool-agent-team`、`packages/client-agent-team`、`packages/agent-team/preset`、`core-skills` 及当次交付；依据 spec.md 指定章节与 issues。
- **行为以源码和测试为准，不以文档为准**；只读，不改代码。
- **两条禁令**：不得把**规划中**的功能（accountable/transfer/accept-close-reopen/sourceThreadRefs）当作已实现；不得把 spec 的**撤回项**当作实现偏差。没有这两条，审查会同时产生大量伪缺陷和噪声。

## 二、核验他人审查：三分法而不是二分法
对一份 15 条外部 review 逐条核实（master 4c72362）的结论分布是：**10 条成立 / 3 条部分成立 / 1 条不成立**。
- 「部分成立」是最有价值的一档：机制对而提示语不准（`self_acceptance_forbidden`）、文件存在只是被 `.scratch/active` ignore 挡在 git 外、文档确未更新但「中英不同步」查无实据（中英对在同提交成对更新）。
- 不成立的一条同样是资产：Client 侧「从已加载窗口推算看板」的回退早已在 07 删除，只剩 `boardEmpty` 文案残留——**核验要把「已修」与「仍未修」明确分开，否则旧结论会被反复重提**。
- 核验要顺手扩围：指出同类但未列出的位置（如 `index.ts:652` 的 body 描述与两处 docs 矛盾）。
- 量化证据优于形容词：`ledger.ts` 6099 行、`rulesVersion` 出现 41 处（严格版本分支 29 处），这类数字是「结构性问题」唯一可证伪的形式。

## 三、缺陷的根因模式（两轮反复出现）
- **规则版本既是行为开关又被当成历史解释器**：v1→v2 采纳后，对 v1 回复做 requestId 重放会用**当前**规则重算 recipients，导致同一回复重试得到不同收件人并抛 `throwRequestCollision`。两个角色必须分离。
- **读写两侧校验强度不对称**：写路径用 `requireProjectMemberActor`，读路径只校验 Workspace participation → 拿到 threadRef 的非成员可读、可 follow，而 follow 会写入成员派生，等于**自助取得 Project 成员身份**。所有读侧入口必须与写侧共用同一成员判定。
- **测试的覆盖形状决定缺陷能否存活**：owner 唤醒 fan-out 缺失之所以长期未被发现，是因为唯一相关测试用了 mention——正好绕开缺口。
- **「标记已读」与「纳入快照」必须同一次操作**：`markRead` 只保留 standing 而丢弃 entries，指向首页 20 条之前的 marker 被消费后，该消息永不进入快照，丢消息是静默的。
- **规则版本切换时，文案与注释必须在同一张 checklist 上**：否则代码对了、说明还在说旧话，下游 agent 会按旧文案推理（`@all` 在 v2 已退化为普通文本，文档仍在宣称它触达整个 Project）。
- **干净检出的隐形雷**：`packages/agent-team/node_modules/zod` 是被 git 跟踪的自指符号链接（内容是机器绝对路径），干净 clone 即损坏——审查必须验证「从零 clone 能否构建」。

## 四、修复后的处置纪律：分类修复 + 保留观察 + 指标兜底
四项修复落地（commit e29ed2c，未 push）的处置方式本身是范式：
- **A｜reopen 恢复 accountable follow**：新 reopen 用 `refollowedMembers` 判别，旧记录保持 marker-only、**不升规则版本**——修 bug 不应顺带触发规则迁移。
- **B｜提醒按当前 durable 条件过滤**：读取时过滤，不改写 marker、不重查 idle，避免修复引入新的写放大。
- **C｜Agent idle ≥30min 与 error 清 idle 保持原状，继续试用观察**——机制可疑但证据不足时，先观察而不是改。
- **D｜文档、升级说明、runbook、`boardEmpty`、recovery 文案、统计脚本一并完成**。

验证判据要真实：真实 SQLite 副本 24625 条重放通过、18 条旧 reopen 兼容、1285 测试与浏览器 8/8 通过。

## 五、闭环的最后一步：用基线指标替代印象
修复不是终点。spec §11 的试用节奏曾在 06–09 一起上线时被跳过，代价是**指标无法归因**。正确收尾：用在线备份出的新 SQLite 副本跑 `scripts/team-trial-metrics.ts`，对比上线前基线（11 条 Agent 回复 / 0 条 Agent 间、4 次 accept-close 全 Human、0 条非 owner 主对话发言、5 条提醒 / 0 条失效未读），并对 `staleUnreadSamples` 与已消费提醒人工判定误报；**绝不打开真实账本**。同时，08 的 Task accountability 工具侧（transfer、accept/close/reopen、`team_message.start` 的 accountable 与 sourceThreadRefs、按动作强制参数口袋）已实现并全量验证（tool-agent-team 87/87、vitest 1247 通过），核验时须把它视为「已落地」而非「规划中」。

**总判据**：审查要能分辨「规划中 / 已实现 / 已修」，修复要能分辨「必改 / 留着观察」，收尾要能分辨「感觉变好了」与「基线指标变了」。

81	## 临时材料和 UI 证据
82	
83	`.scratch/local/`、`.scratch/active/`、`artifacts/` 和 `artifacts/browser/` 被 Git 忽略。临时日志、agent handoff、下载物、调试截图和日常 browser test 输出放在那里，不进入归档。工作项结束时从 `active/` 移入 `archive/YYYY-MM/<work>/`，归档结果进入 Git 历史。
84	
85	UI 改动需要真实浏览器自检时，`npm run test:browser` 会把本次截图写入 `artifacts/browser/`。它们用于审查本次改动，不是自动视觉回归基线，也不会改动 Git 工作区。只有人工确认能说明已完成工作项验收结论的少量代表图，才复制进对应归档的 `archive/YYYY-MM/<work>/validation/`；每张图都必须在同目录 README 中说明证明的验收点和复跑命令。一个浏览器 journey 跨多个 UI ticket 时，可以像本仓库一样集中保存。
86	
87	详细 UI 改动检查和证据选择规则见 [`../docs/development/generated-and-seams.zh.md`](../docs/development/generated-and-seams.zh.md)。

# 工作资料目录索引

`.scratch/` 保存跨会话工作项的设计快照、研究、实施 tickets、原型和可复查的里程碑证据。它不定义当前产品行为、公开 API、稳定维护流程或架构边界；这些以 `packages/`、测试、package README 和 `../docs/` 为准。

**怎么在这里工作（工作项结构、ticket 骨架、Team 流程对接、生命周期）见 [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)。**

## 目录

```text
.scratch/
├── active/                 # 尚未结束的工作项（Git 忽略）
├── archive/YYYY-MM/<work>/ # 已完成工作项的历史资料（进 Git）
└── local/                  # Git 忽略的私人草稿和临时输出
```

## 当前工作项入口

未结束的工作项位于 `active/<work>/`（Git 忽略，不随仓库分发），本索引不列其中的本地条目；工作项结束时移入 `archive/YYYY-MM/`，其 README 会被追加到下面的已归档清单。

Contents of /home/yu/projects/dsh-agent-team/.scratch/AGENTS.md:

# .scratch Work Rules

This subtree holds cross-session work items: design snapshots, research, implementation tickets, prototypes, and acceptance evidence. It is not an implementation or API authority — current behavior is defined by `packages/` source and tests, and maintenance rules by [`../docs/AGENTS.md`](../docs/AGENTS.md). This file only governs how to work here.

## Work-item structure

Each `active/<work>/` is one directory with a short `README.md` as its single continuation entry, covering five items: status, last-checked date, current frontier (who is doing what and what is blocked), completion conditions, and the formal-doc exit.

```
active/<work>/
├── README.md      # continuation entry (the five items above)
├── spec.md        # confirmed decision snapshot — written once discussion converges
├── issues/        # tracer-bullet implementation tickets, one file per ticket
│   ├── 01-<slug>.md
│   └── 02-<slug>.md
├── materials/     # research and external material (keep only what is worth re-reading)
└── validation/    # human-confirmed acceptance evidence (see the development doc)
```

## Ticket discipline

Each `issues/NN-<slug>.md` uses a fixed skeleton, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first):

```markdown
# NN — title

**What to build:** the end-to-end behavior this ticket demonstrably delivers once done (user perspective, not a layered task list)
**Blocked by:** the tickets blocking it, or "None — can start immediately"
**Status:** pending | ready | in-progress | complete

- [ ] acceptance criterion 1
- [ ] acceptance criterion 2
```

- **Vertical slices**: each ticket cuts one narrow, complete path through every layer (schema → API → UI → tests), independently verifiable when done; no horizontal division of labor by layer.
- **Self-contained tickets**: each ticket can start in a new context without reading the whole work-item history. Avoid concrete file paths and code snippets (they go stale); exception: decision-dense fragments from prototypes (state machines, type shapes) may be inlined with their source noted.
- **Frontier workflow**: tickets whose blockers are all done form the frontier and are ready to start; a serial chain runs top to bottom. Tickets that are written but still carry unfinished blockers stay **pending**, so `ready` always means startable now.
- **Wide-refactor exception**: when one mechanical change's blast radius covers the whole repository, do not force it into a tracer bullet — order it as expand–contract: expand first (old and new coexist), migrate in batches, then contract (delete the old form).

## Lifecycle

- **Closing a work item**: close or delete unfinished tickets → move durable conclusions into the `../docs/` maintained documents → delete process material without provenance value → move into `archive/YYYY-MM/`.
- **Archive is history**: archived states and terminology only represent the working context of their time and never override current implementation; do not rewrite archives to match new code.
- **Transient artifacts**: logs, debug screenshots, and downloads go in `local/` or `artifacts/` (gitignored), never into active or archive.

## Version control

- **Active does not enter version history**: while a work item is open, its `active/<work>/` directory is gitignored working material. Force-add it (`git add -f`) only when a reviewer must see it.
- **Archive enters history on close**: when a work item closes, move it into `archive/YYYY-MM/` and amend that move into the commit(s) that deliver the work, so the archive records what actually shipped instead of sitting in a scratch-only commit at the tip.

## Directory index

See [README.md](README.md).

1	# @contexera/dsh-agent-team
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	The Host capability for one Agent Team in a dshHome. `ctx.agentTeam` owns the append-only operation ledger, reconstructs the current collaboration projection, and is the lifecycle owner for member Agents managed by the same capability. Thread Attention and the Member Inbox are durable Host projections. When unread state changes, this package sends one bounded, coalesced context notification through the Agent's public safe-boundary API; it never interrupts an active request or acts as a Session delivery worker. The [Agent Team architecture note](../../.scratch/archive/2026-08/m1/design/agent-notes/2026-08-15-agent-team-operation-ledger.md) owns the persistence and package-topology decisions.
6	
7	## Service contract
8	
9	The Service owns its SQLite-backed DomainFacility and consumes `ctx.workspaceRegistry`, `ctx.agents`, `ctx.agentDefaultModel`, `ctx.agentPresets`, `ctx.tools`, `ctx.tokenMeter`, `ctx.sessionProjections`, and `ctx.sessionPersistence`. It opens the versioned `agent_team` Domain before Cordis publishes `ctx.agentTeam`. The first boot appends one `team/initialized` operation for the stable Human Member; later boots replay the same operation and do not append another record.
10	
11	`status()` returns the current durable sequence, operation count, project count, Agent Member count, and Human Member ref. It performs no model request and no storage write. `validateLedger()` checks the package-owned projection against the durable operation table. The invariant companion re-derives that whole table at mount — an unreplayable ledger fails startup — but adopts the record-level replay the ledger constructor already ran while nothing has committed since, gated on the record count, head sequence, and head operation id, which only the operations table's single writer can change. Any commit in between, and every later validation, replays the durable records again. Afterwards the invariant re-derives once per burst of commits, after the committing call has returned, so a Thread read never waits on an O(ledger) replay; a divergence is logged where it is detected and re-raised on every later commit until a replay comes back clean.
12	
13	Every operation record carries a positive global sequence, unique operation and request ids, an actor snapshot, and the previous operation id. Replay rejects invalid record fields, table-key/id mismatches, sequence gaps, broken previous links, repeated ids, and invalid state transitions. An identical request-id retry returns the original receipt; a changed payload with the same request id rejects.
14	
15	One durable record stores progress instead of the projection it reported. A `team/thread-read` receipt carries the Workspace, Member, Thread ref, optional Task ref, read watermark, and Inbox delta; the Thread, its facts, the anchor, the reader's Attention, and the unread count left behind are re-derived from the projection on every replay. Records written before this form froze that whole picture beside the delta: one strict union accepts both shapes, the legacy record keeps its own full derivation as its expected value, and loading normalizes and validates it without rewriting a stored byte. A record that fits neither shape — a receipt carrying a picture field, a legacy record missing the Task it belongs to or one of its facts — fails the domain open rather than being guessed at. An identical retry of a committed read returns the original receipt with the picture the current projection derives.
16	
17	## Durability and lifecycle
18	
19	`storage-domain` validates every record at the durable read boundary and rejects a backend unit stamped with another version. The Team updates its projection only after `KvTable.put()` resolves. Its Fiber owns the Domain handle; disposal rejects new Service calls through Cordis removal, drains accepted Domain writes, and closes the backend unit before the name can reopen.
20	
21	Member creation commits one stable Member/session/Workspace/preset/private-memory identity before unpublished Agent setup. The creation Workspace is recorded as the Member's creation site; further Workspaces are joined and left through the participation operations (`team/member-workspace-joined`/`team/member-workspace-left`), which grant collaboration immediately without moving the Session. Setup mounts the selected preset and validates its marked `team_message` plus all seven Team tools before publication. Failure leaves only that Member unavailable. Suspend waits for the owned `AgentHandle` to stop; resume and Host remount restore the exact persisted session.
22	
23	Archival is the reversible third state between suspend and remove, for Members and Projects alike. `archiveMember` commits `team/member-archived`, disposes the live session while keeping private memory and the Session log on disk, archives the Session from grouping surfaces, and releases the Member's active Claims with public `claims_released` Activities plus Attention/marker cleanup. `archiveProject` commits `team/project-archived` with the same release shape across every owner on the Project's Threads. Memberships survive both forms — hidden state, not departure. Archived entities are gone from every Team API surface: projections, ref resolution (their Task refs stop resolving, so message bodies render plain text), and ref-addressed reads (`readThread`/`threadHistory`/`threadObservations`/`listClaims` reject with an explicit archived error) — while the facts stay complete in the ledger for replay and a future restore; that boundary is the archival-vs-remove divide. Removal from archived stays available as the data hygiene path; there is no restore entry point yet (mirroring archived dsh sessions).
24	
25	Members optionally carry durable capability intent (`capabilities.tools.allow`, `capabilities.skills.allow`). It flows verbatim through every lifecycle operation, replays unchanged after Host restart, and commits without known-name validation so Harness upgrades can never break old ledgers; divergence from known names surfaces at activation as derived, non-persisted `capabilityWarnings`. `tools.allow` is a deliberate interface reservation: it has no UI write path today. Edits are partial like `model`: an omitted field keeps the stored value and an explicit `null` clears it, so a caller that does not manage capabilities can simply leave the field out.
26	
27	Every Member is restricted to its preset tools plus `working_directory`, even without `tools.allow`. An allow-list only narrows that baseline, retaining the seven Team tools and `working_directory`; out-of-baseline names produce warnings. Late plugin tools are filtered from requests and denied execution; same-name replacements reject request assembly. Other plugins' prompts remain visible and do not block conversation. See [Tools and preset](../../docs/architecture/tools-and-preset.md) for the checks and their limits. Live edits swap restrictions at a turn boundary in the same Session; later lifecycle operations wait behind the edit. Activation failures leave only that Member unavailable.
28	
29	Skills are Member-private: the preset has no shared skill-filesystem row, and the Host registers one provider per Member that scans exactly the plugin's bundled read-only core skills (`packages/agent-team/core-skills/` — the `member-skill-manager` meta skill that owns all skill craft guidance) plus that Member's writable `skills/` directory under its private memory path (default roots excluded). Installing is writing into the Member's own directory — directory form `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with optional references and scripts, or a flat `.md` — and there is deliberately no upload Remote. The persona itself only states the private-space physical facts; the meta skill's description routes skill-management work to it. `skills.allow` filters the catalog through a live selection swap on the mounted provider at the same turn boundary; the filesystem watcher feeds discovery after a self-install.
30	
31	Every team-managed session records `danger-full-access`. Session cwd remains the Workspace path, while private memory lives under `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/members/<memberId>/`. An untitled Member session is named with its handle through the session-title service, so the ordinary Session list shows the Member identity; an explicit rename or any earlier title always wins. The isolated `team-member` preset also provides coding tools including model-facing web search, Workspace instruction discovery, and Team protocol guidance. The host owns the shared Web service and provider; the preset mounts only the model-facing web tool. Its lowercase `memory.md` is a bounded 16 KiB reference index: missing context receives the full index, while later file edits produce a short stale-copy notice with current usage, not another full copy. Identity, ownership, and Workspace participation update separately; [Member context injection](../../docs/team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md#member-context-injection) defines recovery. `notes/` stays on-demand through filesystem tools. Over-budget indexes receive a maintenance warning, not silent truncation. Ordinary sessions and forks receive no Team identity or private-memory context. At Host startup every enabled Member's private memory is provisioned and an `inactive` Member's is removed with its Session archived; directories the replayed ledger does not reference are never pruned, so leftovers from a discarded ledger stay on disk for the operator. Both that removal and the activation-time migration of a pre-fix colon directory act only on paths inside the running process's own `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/members/`: a recorded path naming a different DSH home (an isolated test home, a second instance) is refused with a warning rather than renamed or deleted, because acting on it would take a Member's real private memory out of its home.
32	
33	Adding a Member to a Project grants future read/send/claim authority but injects no historical Messages into the member session. A Thread is created by `startThread`, never by a Main stream message: a started Thread is a discussion, or a Task when `kind: 'task'` asks for one, and a Human can later promote a taskless Thread by atomically adding its Task overlay and a structured `promote` Task activity. Thread Attention starts when a Thread is created, a Claim is created, or a member follows — never from a mention or a reply, which deliver one direct marker and leave Attention alone. Ordinary unread is derived from Attention; structured mentions create durable direct markers, while terminal Task changes retain sparse Activity markers for affected followers after Attention ends. `team_inbox` and Thread reads are Host projections, not Session inbox contents. A direct mention context includes its Message body and source; Task/Claim changes — including promotion — include the complete immutable event; ordinary unread carries a body-free Thread-first route. Pending hints are coalesced, ignored hints do not loop, and resume/error recovery derives a new hint from durable unread state. For recoverable service failures, the Host wakes a Member after each of the first two consecutive `agent/error` occurrences, then leaves the third failure for the operator; only a clean turn resets that run.
34	
35	Member replies require the exact current Thread revision and atomically update Message and Thread facts. `threadRef` is the primary collaboration identity; the Host also resolves `taskRef` to its taskful Thread, while Task/Claim operations remain Task-ref based. Each tool action's address requirements are defined in the [tool contract](../../docs/team-collaboration/tools.md). [Mutation fences](../../docs/team-collaboration/boundaries.md#mutation-fences) defines the unread and revision checks: exact, complete Thread Message and Activity facts from a Team notice or tool result can satisfy the context requirement without acknowledging unread. A Main stream post has no token and follows the same context rule. A DM cannot supply Thread evidence. Complete rejections can support reconsideration; partial results require reading. A closed Task rejects replies and new Attention; reopening restores the Task without restoring prior Attention. Taskless Threads still support replies, follow, mentions, Inbox, read, and history, but have no Claims or Task-resolution path. Under rules version 2 a mention delivers one direct marker and never starts Attention, and a reply carries the parent's author into the recipient set the same way. Every addressable recipient is delivered — a Member the Thread has never carried included — and nothing follows as a side effect; there is no invitation step and no undelivered remainder to report. Mentions are authored in the Message body as `@Handle` and resolved by the Host against the Project's addressable names; the body is the sole delivery authority, and no recipient list travels with the request. Message facts carry the resolved refs, and the Client renders mention chips only for those Members. Claim/done/release and Task changes are ordered host-authored Activities. Active Claims exclude only the same normalized Direction; different Directions can run concurrently. Task state is derived from Claims unless Human acceptance or closure overrides it. Close releases active Claims and clears Thread Attention atomically. Member removal marks the member inactive, releases owned active Claims, clears its Attention and direct markers, and archives the session after the durable commit. Message and Activity facts share one bounded sequence cursor.
36	
37	`changes({ scope? }, signal?)` returns an `AsyncIterable<{ version: number }>` through a streaming Remote. It emits the current baseline, then matching workspace/project/thread/presence invalidations; omitting scope observes shared projections but not presence. A paused consumer retains only the latest pending version; cancellation or Host disposal closes the stream. The Client must reread projections on every baseline, even when the version is unchanged or lower after a restart. See [architecture](../../docs/architecture/host-authority.md) for scope/version and recovery semantics. Thread reads change only private read state: they wake no scope, and a read with no unread or markers to consume appends no operation. After a commit, Inbox hints are recomputed only for affected Members.
38	
39	Agent Thread and Main stream reads restore missing original background from current Session visibility, explicitly omit already-visible Message bodies and complete Activity events, and acknowledge only the prefix the tool can render within its output ceiling; a Thread read receipt stores that bound, while older receipts keep the default batch. Long bodies return in ordered parts, and repeating the same request resumes at the missing segment. Human reads, Remote parameters, and durable receipt interpretation are otherwise unchanged; [the reading contract](../../docs/team-collaboration/tools.md#team_thread) defines the presentation.
40	
41	M1 supports one Host writer. The ledger is permanent and has no snapshot or compaction path.
42	
43	## Composition
44	
45	The bundle consumes the Host's existing singleton providers; it does not mount replacements for `agents`, default model selection, `tools`, `fs`, `sandboxPolicy`, Session store/persistence, or Workspace registry. Its private SQLite DomainFacility does not replace the Host's global storage service, so toggling the bundle does not rebuild unrelated storage consumers. Load those Host services once, then mount this Service and its invariant companion. The Team Web Client is the only Human control surface.
46	
47	A team-enabled preset registers the seven tools in its own agent scope and marks the `team_message` definition with `markAgentTeamPreset()`. Preset rows must resolve `ctx.agentTeam` when executing, not statically inject it: the Host mounts member presets while it restores Members during its own activation, so a row that declares `agentTeam` as a dependency cannot activate and fails every startup restore. Duplicate scoped tool names fail during unpublished setup and make only that Member unavailable. Duplicate Host service providers remain a composition error and should be removed rather than layered.
48	
49	Member context has two mechanisms and no model tool. The preset's `member-compaction-engine` delegates summaries and durable reduction to the Harness, while Team bounds input and output before each request; [`../../docs/team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md`](../../docs/team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md) owns those numbers. A generation swap is a Host decision at a wake boundary: `team-context-management.ts` waits for true idle, rechecks the owned-jobs guard, commits the idempotent `team/member-session-recycled` operation (Host actor), retires the old Session (dispose and archive, never delete), and activates a fresh one parented at the one it replaces. Identity, model, private memory, skills, Claims, and Attention survive, and process state is reconstructible from the durable log after a crash. No Remote write renews, rolls over, or otherwise resets a Member's context.
50	
51	## Model Experience
52	
53	### Host collaboration state
54	
55	#### What the model sees
56	
57	An enabled Member may receive one bounded, coalesced context notification after durable unread work appears. Structured direct mentions include their Message body and source; Task/Claim Activities include their complete immutable event; ordinary unread includes only a Thread-first route and counts, with a Task overlay where present. The notification is queued at the Agent's safe step boundary, so active model requests and tools are not interrupted. It routes the common path directly to `team_thread.read`; the model uses `team_inbox` only when it needs to triage remaining Threads. Missing direct signals are ranked ahead of ordinary counts; [`../../docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md`](../../docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md) owns the notice shape, order, and budget.
58	
59	#### Token effect
60	
61	The ledger, projection, and Human status reads add no model tokens.
62	
63	#### KV Cache effect
64	
65	The Host ledger and Human status reads do not alter model requests or cache reuse.
66	
67	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
68	
69	- **Single Host writer** — concurrent processes over one dshHome are unsupported; operation serialization is process-local.
70	- **Permanent ledger** — M1 provides neither snapshots nor compaction, so storage grows with committed collaboration facts.
71	- **No remote provider seam** — the package combines the capability definition and its only implementation until a real remote Consumer requires another Provider.
72	- **No Session migration of its own** — Member Sessions ride the Host's Session persistence and its released-format migration chain; this package provides no Team ledger or Member Session migration, compatibility read, or fallback.
73
