The creation Workspace is recorded as the Member's creation site; further Workspaces are joined and left through the participation operations (`team/member-workspace-joined`/`team/member-workspace-left`), which grant collaboration immediately without moving the Session. Setup mounts the selected preset and validates its marked `team_message` plus all seven Team tools before publication. Failure leaves only that Member unavailable. Suspend waits for the owned `AgentHandle` to stop; resume and Host remount restore the exact persisted session.

Archival is the reversible third state between suspend and remove, for Members and Projects alike. `archiveMember` commits `team/member-archived`, disposes the live session while keeping private memory and the Session log on disk, archives the Session from grouping surfaces, and releases the Member's active Claims with public `claims_released` Activities plus Attention/marker cleanup. `archiveProject` commits `team/project-archived` with the same release shape across every owner on the Project's Threads. Memberships survive both forms — hidden state, not departure. Archived entities are gone from every Team API surface: projections, ref resolution (their Task refs stop resolving, so message bodies render plain text), and ref-addressed reads (`readThread`/`threadHistory`/`threadObservations`/`listClaims` reject with an explicit archived error) — while the facts stay complete in the ledger for replay and a future restore; that boundary is the archival-vs-remove divide. Removal from archived stays available as the data hygiene path; there is no restore entry point yet (mirroring archived dsh sessions).

Members optionally carry durable capability intent (`capabilities.tools.allow`, `capabilities.skills.allow`). It flows verbatim through every lifecycle operation, replays unchanged after Host restart, and commits without known-name validation so Harness upgrades can never break old ledgers; divergence from known names surfaces at activation as derived, non-persisted `capabilityWarnings`. `tools.allow` is a deliberate interface reservation: it has no UI write path today. Edits are partial like `model`: an omitted field keeps the stored value and an explicit `null` clears it, so a caller that does not manage capabilities can simply leave the field out.

Every Member is restricted to its preset tools plus `working_directory`, even without `tools.allow`. An allow-list only narrows that baseline, retaining the seven Team tools and `working_directory`; out-of-baseline names produce warnings. Late plugin tools are filtered from requests and denied execution; same-name replacements reject request assembly. Other plugins' prompts remain visible and do not block conversation. See [Tools and preset](../../docs/architecture/tools-and-preset.md) for the checks and their limits. Live edits swap restrictions at a turn boundary in the same Session; later lifecycle operations wait behind the edit. Activation failures leave only that Member unavailable.

Skills are Member-private: the preset has no shared skill-filesystem row, and the Host registers one provider per Member that scans exactly the plugin's bundled read-only core skills (`packages/agent-team/core-skills/` — the `member-skill-manager` meta skill that owns all skill craft guidance) plus that Member's writable `skills/` directory under its private memory path (default roots excluded). Installing is writing into the Member's own directory — directory form `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with optional references and scripts, or a flat `.md` — and there is deliberately no upload Remote. The persona itself only states the private-space physical facts; the meta skill's description routes skill-management work to it. `skills.allow` filters the catalog through a live selection swap on the mounted provider at the same turn boundary; the filesystem watcher feeds discovery after a self-install.

Every team-managed session records `danger-full-access`. Session cwd remains the Workspace path, while private memory lives under `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/members/<memberId>/`. An untitled Member session is named with its handle through the session-title service, so the ordinary Session list shows the Member identity; an explicit rename or any earlier title always wins. The isolated `team-member` preset also provides coding tools including model-facing web search, Workspace instruction discovery, and Team protocol guidance. The host owns the shared Web service and provider; the preset mounts only the model-facing web tool. Its lowercase `memory.md` is a bounded 16 KiB reference index: missing context receives the full index, while later file edits produce a short stale-copy notice with current usage, not another full copy. Identity, ownership, and Workspace participation update separately; [Member context injection](../../docs/team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md#member-context-injection) defines recovery. `notes/` stays on-demand through filesystem tools. Over-budget indexes receive a maintenance warning, not silent truncation. Ordinary sessions and forks receive no Team identity or private-memory context. At Host startup every enabled Member's private memory is provisioned and an `inactive` Member's is removed with its Session archived; directories the replayed ledger does not reference are never pruned, so leftovers from a discarded ledger stay on disk for the operator. Both that removal and the activation-time migration of a pre-fix colon directory act only on paths inside the running process's own `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/members/`: a recorded path naming a different DSH home (an isolated test home, a second instance) is refused with a warning rather than renamed or deleted, because acting on it would take a Member's real private memory out of its home.

Adding a Member to a Project grants future read/send/claim authority but injects no historical Messages into the member session. A Thread is created by `startThread`, never by a Main stream message: a started Thread is a discussion, or a Task when `kind: 'task'` asks for one, and a Human can later promote a taskless Thread by atomically adding its Task overlay and a structured `promote` Task activity. Thread Attention starts when a Thread is created, a Claim is created, or a member follows — never from a mention or a reply, which deliver one direct marker and leave Attention alone. Ordinary unread is derived from Attention; structured mentions create durable direct markers, while terminal Task changes retain sparse Activity markers for affected followers after Attention ends. `team_inbox` and Thread reads are Host projections, not Session inbox contents. A direct mention context includes its Message body and source; Task/Claim changes — including promotion — include the complete immutable event; ordinary unread carries a body-free Thread-first route. Pending hints are coalesced, ignored hints do not loop, and resume/error recovery derives a new hint from durable unread state. For recoverable service failures, the Host wakes a Member after each of the first two consecutive `agent/error` occurrences, then leaves the third failure for the operator; only a clean turn resets that run.

Member replies require the exact current Thread revision and atomically update Message and Thread facts. `threadRef` is the primary collaboration identity; the Host also resolves `taskRef` to its taskful Thread, while Task/Claim operations remain Task-ref based. Each tool action's address requirements are defined in the [tool contract](../../docs/team-collaboration/tools.md). [Mutation fences](../../docs/team-collaboration/boundaries.md#mutation-fences) defines the unread and revision checks: exact, complete Thread Message and Activity facts from a Team notice or tool result can satisfy the context requirement without acknowledging unread. A Main stream post has no token and follows the same context rule. A DM cannot supply Thread evidence. Complete rejections can support reconsideration; partial results require reading. A closed Task rejects replies and new Attention; reopening restores the Task without restoring prior Attention. Taskless Threads still support replies, follow, mentions, Inbox, read, and history, but have no Claims or Task-resolution path. Under rules version 2 a mention delivers one direct marker and never starts Attention, and a reply carries the parent's author into the recipient set the same way. Every addressable recipient is delivered — a Member the Thread has never carried included — and nothing follows as a side effect; there is no invitation step and no undelivered remainder to report. Mentions are authored in the Message body as `@Handle` and resolved by the Host against the Project's addressable names; the body is the sole delivery authority, and no recipient list travels with the request. Message facts carry the resolved refs, and the Client renders mention chips only for those Members. Claim/done/release and Task changes are ordered host-authored Activities. Active Claims exclude only the same normalized Direction; different Directions can run concurrently. Task state is derived from Claims unless Human acceptance or closure overrides it. Close releases active Claims and clears Thread Attention atomically. Member removal marks the member inactive, releases owned active Claims, clears its Attention and direct markers, and archives the session after the durable commit. Message and Activity facts share one bounded sequence cursor.

`changes({ scope? }, signal?)` returns an `AsyncIterable<{ version: number }>` through a streaming Remote. It emits the current baseline, then matching workspace/project/thread/presence invalidations; omitting scope observes shared projections but not presence. A paused consumer retains only the latest pending version; cancellation or Host disposal closes the stream. The Client must reread projections on every baseline, even when the version is unchanged or lower after a restart. See [architecture](../../docs/architecture/host-authority.md) for scope/version and recovery semantics. Thread reads change only private read state: they wake no scope, and a read with no unread or markers to consume appends no operation. After a commit, Inbox hints are recomputed only for affected Members.

Agent Thread and Main stream reads restore missing original background from current Session visibility, explicitly omit already-visible Message bodies and complete Activity events, and acknowledge only the prefix the tool can render within its output ceiling; a Thread read receipt stores that bound, while older receipts keep the default batch. Long bodies return in ordered parts, and repeating the same request resumes at the missing segment. Human reads, Remote parameters, and durable receipt interpretation are otherwise unchanged; [the reading contract](../../docs/team-collaboration/tools.md#team_thread) defines the presentation.

M1 supports one Host writer. The ledger is permanent and has no snapshot or compaction path.

## Composition

The bundle consumes the Host's existing singleton providers; it does not mount replacements for `agents`, default model selection, `tools`, `fs`, `sandboxPolicy`, Session store/persistence, or Workspace registry. Its private SQLite DomainFacility does not replace the Host's global storage service, so toggling the bundle does not rebuild unrelated storage consumers. Load those Host services once, then mount this Service and its invariant companion. The Team Web Client is the only Human control surface.

A team-enabled preset registers the seven tools in its own agent scope and marks the `team_message` definition with `markAgentTeamPreset()`. Preset rows must resolve `ctx.agentTeam` when executing, not statically inject it: the Host mounts member presets while it restores Members during its own activation, so a row that declares `agentTeam` as a dependency cannot activate and fails every startup restore. Duplicate scoped tool names fail during unpublished setup and make only that Member unavailable. Duplicate Host service providers remain a composition error and should be removed rather than layered.

Member context has two mechanisms and no model tool. The preset's `member-compaction-engine` delegates summaries and durable reduction to the Harness, while Team bounds input and output before each request; [`../../docs/team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md`](../../docs/team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md) owns those numbers. A generation swap is a Host decision at a wake boundary: `team-context-management.ts` waits for true idle, rechecks the owned-jobs guard, commits the idempotent `team/member-session-recycled` operation (Host actor), retires the old Session (dispose and archive, never delete), and activates a fresh one parented at the one it replaces. Identity, model, private memory, skills, Claims, and Attention survive, and process state is reconstructible from the durable log after a crash. No Remote write renews, rolls over, or otherwise resets a Member's context.

## Model Experience

### Host collaboration state

#### What the model sees

An enabled Member may receive one bounded, coalesced context notification after durable unread work appears. Structured direct mentions include their Message body and source; Task/Claim Activities include their complete immutable event; ordinary unread includes only a Thread-first route and counts, with a Task overlay where present. The notification is queued at the Agent's safe step boundary, so active model requests and tools are not interrupted. It routes the common path directly to `team_thread.read`; the model uses `team_inbox` only when it needs to triage remaining Threads. Missing direct signals are ranked ahead of ordinary counts; [`../../docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md`](../../docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md) owns the notice shape, order, and budget.

#### Token effect

The ledger, projection, and Human status reads add no model tokens.

#### KV Cache effect

The Host ledger and Human status reads do not alter model requests or cache reuse.

## Known Limitations and Deferred Work

- **Single Host writer** — concurrent processes over one dshHome are unsupported; operation serialization is process-local.
- **Permanent ledger** — M1 provides neither snapshots nor compaction, so storage grows with committed collaboration facts.
- **No remote provider seam** — the package combines the capability definition and its only implementation until a real remote Consumer requires another Provider.
- **No Session migration of its own** — Member Sessions ride the Host's Session persistence and its released-format migration chain; this package provides no Team ledger or Member Session migration, compatibility read, or fallback.

CHANGELOG.md:29:- Event-evaluated Task reminders cover review backlog and stalled work. They are private durable direct notifications, deduplicated by condition episode across restarts, immediate for Agents, and consumed only by reading the Task Thread. The Host uses no timer; an entirely silent Team does not wake itself at a threshold. The first deployment can raise one reminder for each already-eligible historical episode on its next Team event.
CHANGELOG.md:36:- Complete Thread Message rejections provide the facts and current token needed to reconsider a write without a mandatory extra read. The Host verifies exact Team source, Thread/Message identity, and the actual Session text; summaries and truncated results cannot satisfy the check. Partial rejections supply no token, and neither notifications nor rejections acknowledge unread work.
CHANGELOG.md:57:- The follow control reads the Human's own row out of the follower set instead of asking whether the set is non-empty. The set holds every Member whose Attention is on the Thread, so while any Agent still followed, the Human's unfollow left the button pressed with the pressed fill while its word read 「关注」; the same reading also made a press on a Thread only an Agent followed answer "already following". The Human's own Attention and notification gate were never wrong — only the Client's identity test was.
CHANGELOG.md:86:- A cold Member generation is replaced automatically before a wake reaches it. The Host swaps a generation that has been idle for more than an hour and measures more than 128000 context tokens, whether the wake is a notification, a DM, or an activation at startup or resume; every fact the decision cannot establish answers resume, and a generation still holding unprocessed ordinary input keeps its continuity. Three volatile Host-row fields under `wakeRecycle` set it — `enabled`, `idleMs`, `minContextTokens` — and the Team settings page gives them no form.
CHANGELOG.md:87:- A swap no longer strands the input it was racing. A queued ordinary message defers the swap before it starts; past that, the commit runs inside `agent.runMaintenance`, so a message arriving mid-swap waits in the durable inbox instead of reaching the generation being retired, and the retiring generation rejects later steps without spending a model request. Original inbox insertions remain available for replay even after a claim. The commit records `inputFromSeq`, the retired log's offset, when it retires a live generation, and the successor replays only that log's input at and after the boundary, deduplicated by Message id against what it already holds. Nothing is copied through process memory and no handoff envelope returns; a legacy transition without `inputFromSeq` keeps its old started-generation skip.
CHANGELOG.md:235:- Fixed archived Channels leaking their Threads into the Inbox: archival ends participation as well as notification.
CHANGELOG.md:295:- Fixed early-accept notifications carrying an empty finished-claim clause.

packages/agent-team/README.md:5:The Host capability for one Agent Team in a dshHome. `ctx.agentTeam` owns the append-only operation ledger, reconstructs the current collaboration projection, and is the lifecycle owner for member Agents managed by the same capability. Thread Attention and the Member Inbox are durable Host projections. When unread state changes, this package sends one bounded, coalesced context notification through the Agent's public safe-boundary API; it never interrupts an active request or acts as a Session delivery worker. The [Agent Team architecture note](../../.scratch/archive/2026-08/m1/design/agent-notes/2026-08-15-agent-team-operation-ledger.md) owns the persistence and package-topology decisions.
packages/agent-team/README.md:11:`status()` returns the current durable sequence, operation count, project count, Agent Member count, and Human Member ref. It performs no model request and no storage write. `validateLedger()` checks the package-owned projection against the durable operation table. The invariant companion re-derives that whole table at mount — an unreplayable ledger fails startup — but adopts the record-level replay the ledger constructor already ran while nothing has committed since, gated on the record count, head sequence, and head operation id, which only the operations table's single writer can change. Any commit in between, and every later validation, replays the durable records again. Afterwards the invariant re-derives once per burst of commits, after the committing call has returned, so a Thread read never waits on an O(ledger) replay; a divergence is logged where it is detected and re-raised on every later commit until a replay comes back clean.
packages/agent-team/README.md:45:The bundle consumes the Host's existing singleton providers; it does not mount replacements for `agents`, default model selection, `tools`, `fs`, `sandboxPolicy`, Session store/persistence, or Workspace registry. Its private SQLite DomainFacility does not replace the Host's global storage service, so toggling the bundle does not rebuild unrelated storage consumers. Load those Host services once, then mount this Service and its invariant companion. The Team Web Client is the only Human control surface.
packages/agent-team/README.md:57:An enabled Member may receive one bounded, coalesced context notification after durable unread work appears. Structured direct mentions include their Message body and source; Task/Claim Activities include their complete immutable event; ordinary unread includes only a Thread-first route and counts, with a Task overlay where present. The notification is queued at the Agent's safe step boundary, so active model requests and tools are not interrupted. It routes the common path directly to `team_thread.read`; the model uses `team_inbox` only when it needs to triage remaining Threads. Missing direct signals are ranked ahead of ordinary counts; [`../../docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md`](../../docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md) owns the notice shape, order, and budget.

packages/agent-team/README.zh.md:35:Member reply 必须携带准确的当前 Thread revision，并在一个 operation 内更新 Message 和 Thread facts。`threadRef` 是协作主身份；Host 也能将 `taskRef` 解析到对应的 taskful Thread，而 Task/Claim 操作仍以 Task ref 为准。各工具 action 的地址要求见[工具契约](../../docs/team-collaboration/tools.zh.md)。[Mutation fences](../../docs/team-collaboration/boundaries.zh.md#mutation-fences) 定义未读与 revision 检查：Team 通知或工具结果中完整、身份准确的 Thread Message 与 Activity 可满足上下文条件，但不确认未读。Main stream post 没有令牌，也遵循同样的上下文规则。DM 不能提供 Thread 凭据。完整拒绝可支持重新考虑，部分结果仍须读取。Closed Task 拒绝 reply 和新的 Attention；reopen 恢复 Task，但不恢复之前的 Attention。taskless Thread 仍支持 reply、follow、mention、Inbox、read 和 history，但没有 Claim 或 Task resolution path。规则版本 2 下，mention 只投递一个 direct marker 且绝不开始 Attention；回复以同样方式把父消息作者并入收件人集合。每个可寻址的收件人都会送达——包括该 Thread 从未承载过的 Member——且不因此开始任何 Attention；没有邀请环节，也没有未送达的残余需要报告。mention 在 Message 正文里以 `@Handle` 撰写，由 Host 按 Project 的可寻址名字解析；正文是唯一的送达依据，请求不携带收件人列表。Message fact 携带解析后的 refs，Client 只为这些 Member 渲染 mention chip。claim/done/release 和 Task change 是有序的 host-authored Activity。Active Claim 只排斥相同的 normalized Direction；不同 Direction 可以并行。Task status 从 Claims 派生，Human accept/close 是覆盖事实。Close 原子释放 active Claims 并清除 Thread Attention。Member remove 原子标记 inactive、释放 owned active Claims、清除该成员的 Attention 和 direct markers，再归档 session。Message 与 Activity facts 共用一个有界 sequence cursor。
packages/agent-team/README.zh.md:37:`changes({ scope? }, signal?)` 通过流式 Remote 返回 `AsyncIterable<{ version: number }>`。先发送当前基线，之后发送匹配的 workspace/project/thread/presence 通知；省略 scope 时观察共享投影，不包含 presence。消费者暂停期间只保留最新待发送版本；取消或 Host 释放时关闭流。Client 必须在每次基线到达时重读投影，即使重启后的版本相同或更低。scope、版本和恢复语义见[架构文档](../../docs/architecture/host-authority.zh.md)。Thread read 只改变私有已读状态，不唤醒任何 scope；没有未读或 marker 可消费时不追加 operation。提交后只为受影响的 Members 重算 Inbox hints。

CHANGELOG.md:29:- Event-evaluated Task reminders cover review backlog and stalled work. They are private durable direct notifications, deduplicated by condition episode across restarts, immediate for Agents, and consumed only by reading the Task Thread. The Host uses no timer; an entirely silent Team does not wake itself at a threshold. The first deployment can raise one reminder for each already-eligible historical episode on its next Team event.
CHANGELOG.md:36:- Complete Thread Message rejections provide the facts and current token needed to reconsider a write without a mandatory extra read. The Host verifies exact Team source, Thread/Message identity, and the actual Session text; summaries and truncated results cannot satisfy the check. Partial rejections supply no token, and neither notifications nor rejections acknowledge unread work.
CHANGELOG.md:57:- The follow control reads the Human's own row out of the follower set instead of asking whether the set is non-empty. The set holds every Member whose Attention is on the Thread, so while any Agent still followed, the Human's unfollow left the button pressed with the pressed fill while its word read 「关注」; the same reading also made a press on a Thread only an Agent followed answer "already following". The Human's own Attention and notification gate were never wrong — only the Client's identity test was.
CHANGELOG.md:86:- A cold Member generation is replaced automatically before a wake reaches it. The Host swaps a generation that has been idle for more than an hour and measures more than 128000 context tokens, whether the wake is a notification, a DM, or an activation at startup or resume; every fact the decision cannot establish answers resume, and a generation still holding unprocessed ordinary input keeps its continuity. Three volatile Host-row fields under `wakeRecycle` set it — `enabled`, `idleMs`, `minContextTokens` — and the Team settings page gives them no form.
CHANGELOG.md:87:- A swap no longer strands the input it was racing. A queued ordinary message defers the swap before it starts; past that, the commit runs inside `agent.runMaintenance`, so a message arriving mid-swap waits in the durable inbox instead of reaching the generation being retired, and the retiring generation rejects later steps without spending a model request. Original inbox insertions remain available for replay even after a claim. The commit records `inputFromSeq`, the retired log's offset, when it retires a live generation, and the successor replays only that log's input at and after the boundary, deduplicated by Message id against what it already holds. Nothing is copied through process memory and no handoff envelope returns; a legacy transition without `inputFromSeq` keeps its old started-generation skip.
CHANGELOG.md:235:- Fixed archived Channels leaking their Threads into the Inbox: archival ends participation as well as notification.
CHANGELOG.md:295:- Fixed early-accept notifications carrying an empty finished-claim clause.

83	`.scratch/local/`、`.scratch/active/`、`artifacts/` 和 `artifacts/browser/` 被 Git 忽略。临时日志、agent handoff、下载物、调试截图和日常 browser test 输出放在那里，不进入归档。工作项结束时从 `active/` 移入 `archive/YYYY-MM/<work>/`，归档结果进入 Git 历史。

1	# @contexera/dsh-agent-team
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	The Host capability for one Agent Team in a dshHome. `ctx.agentTeam` owns the append-only operation ledger, reconstructs the current collaboration projection, and is the lifecycle owner for member Agents managed by the same capability. Thread Attention and the Member Inbox are durable Host projections. When unread state changes, this package sends one bounded, coalesced context notification through the Agent's public safe-boundary API; it never interrupts an active request or acts as a Session delivery worker. The [Agent Team architecture note](../../.scratch/archive/2026-08/m1/design/agent-notes/2026-08-15-agent-team-operation-ledger.md) owns the persistence and package-topology decisions.
6	
7	## Service contract
8	
9	The Service owns its SQLite-backed DomainFacility and consumes `ctx.workspaceRegistry`, `ctx.agents`, `ctx.agentDefaultModel`, `ctx.agentPresets`, `ctx.tools`, `ctx.tokenMeter`, `ctx.sessionProjections`, and `ctx.sessionPersistence`. It opens the versioned `agent_team` Domain before Cordis publishes `ctx.agentTeam`. The first boot appends one `team/initialized` operation for the stable Human Member; later boots replay the same operation and do not append another record.
10	
11	`status()` returns the current durable sequence, operation count, project count, Agent Member count, and Human Member ref. It performs no model request and no storage write. `validateLedger()` checks the package-owned projection against the durable operation table. The invariant companion re-derives that whole table at mount — an unreplayable ledger fails startup — but adopts the record-level replay the ledger constructor already ran while nothing has committed since, gated on the record count, head sequence, and head operation id, which only the operations table's single writer can change. Any commit in between, and every later validation, replays the durable records again. Afterwards the invariant re-derives once per burst of commits, after the committing call has returned, so a Thread read never waits on an O(ledger) replay; a divergence is logged where it is detected and re-raised on every later commit until a replay comes back clean.
12	
13	Every operation record carries a positive global sequence, unique operation and request ids, an actor snapshot, and the previous operation id. Replay rejects invalid record fields, table-key/id mismatches, sequence gaps, broken previous links, repeated ids, and invalid state transitions. An identical request-id retry returns the original receipt; a changed payload with the same request id rejects.
14	
15	One durable record stores progress instead of the projection it reported. A `team/thread-read` receipt carries the Workspace, Member, Thread ref, optional Task ref, read watermark, and Inbox delta; the Thread, its facts, the anchor, the reader's Attention, and the unread count left behind are re-derived from the projection on every replay. Records written before this form froze that whole picture beside the delta: one strict union accepts both shapes, the legacy record keeps its own full derivation as its expected value, and loading normalizes and validates it without rewriting a stored byte. A record that fits neither shape — a receipt carrying a picture field, a legacy record missing the Task it belongs to or one of its facts — fails the domain open rather than being guessed at. An identical retry of a committed read returns the original receipt with the picture the current projection derives.
16	
17	## Durability and lifecycle
18	
19	`storage-domain` validates every record at the durable read boundary and rejects a backend unit stamped with another version. The Team updates its projection only after `KvTable.put()` resolves. Its Fiber owns the Domain handle; disposal rejects new Service calls through Cordis removal, drains accepted Domain writes, and closes the backend unit before the name can reopen.
20	
21	Member creation commits one stable Member/session/Workspace/preset/private-memory identity before unpublished Agent setup. The creation Workspace is recorded as the Member's creation site; further Workspaces are joined and left through the participation operations (`team/member-workspace-joined`/`team/member-workspace-left`), which grant collaboration immediately without moving the Session. Setup mounts the selected preset and validates its marked `team_message` plus all seven Team tools before publication. Failure leaves only that Member unavailable. Suspend waits for the owned `AgentHandle` to stop; resume and Host remount restore the exact persisted session.
22	
23	Archival is the reversible third state between suspend and remove, for Members and Projects alike. `archiveMember` commits `team/member-archived`, disposes the live session while keeping private memory and the Session log on disk, archives the Session from grouping surfaces, and releases the Member's active Claims with public `claims_released` Activities plus Attention/marker cleanup. `archiveProject` commits `team/project-archived` with the same release shape across every owner on the Project's Threads. Memberships survive both forms — hidden state, not departure. Archived entities are gone from every Team API surface: projections, ref resolution (their Task refs stop resolving, so message bodies render plain text), and ref-addressed reads (`readThread`/`threadHistory`/`threadObservations`/`listClaims` reject with an explicit archived error) — while the facts stay complete in the ledger for replay and a future restore; that boundary is the archival-vs-remove divide. Removal from archived stays available as the data hygiene path; there is no restore entry point yet (mirroring archived dsh sessions).
24	
25	Members optionally carry durable capability intent (`capabilities.tools.allow`, `capabilities.skills.allow`). It flows verbatim through every lifecycle operation, replays unchanged after Host restart, and commits without known-name validation so Harness upgrades can never break old ledgers; divergence from known names surfaces at activation as derived, non-persisted `capabilityWarnings`. `tools.allow` is a deliberate interface reservation: it has no UI write path today. Edits are partial like `model`: an omitted field keeps the stored value and an explicit `null` clears it, so a caller that does not manage capabilities can simply leave the field out.
26	
27	Every Member is restricted to its preset tools plus `working_directory`, even without `tools.allow`. An allow-list only narrows that baseline, retaining the seven Team tools and `working_directory`; out-of-baseline names produce warnings. Late plugin tools are filtered from requests and denied execution; same-name replacements reject request assembly. Other plugins' prompts remain visible and do not block conversation. See [Tools and preset](../../docs/architecture/tools-and-preset.md) for the checks and their limits. Live edits swap restrictions at a turn boundary in the same Session; later lifecycle operations wait behind the edit. Activation failures leave only that Member unavailable.
28	
29	Skills are Member-private: the preset has no shared skill-filesystem row, and the Host registers one provider per Member that scans exactly the plugin's bundled read-only core skills (`packages/agent-team/core-skills/` — the `member-skill-manager` meta skill that owns all skill craft guidance) plus that Member's writable `skills/` directory under its private memory path (default roots excluded). Installing is writing into the Member's own directory — directory form `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with optional references and scripts, or a flat `.md` — and there is deliberately no upload Remote. The persona itself only states the private-space physical facts; the meta skill's description routes skill-management work to it. `skills.allow` filters the catalog through a live selection swap on the mounted provider at the same turn boundary; the filesystem watcher feeds discovery after a self-install.
30	
31	Every team-managed session records `danger-full-access`. Session cwd remains the Workspace path, while private memory lives under `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/members/<memberId>/`. An untitled Member session is named with its handle through the session-title service, so the ordinary Session list shows the Member identity; an explicit rename or any earlier title always wins. The isolated `team-member` preset also provides coding tools including model-facing web search, Workspace instruction discovery, and Team protocol guidance. The host owns the shared Web service and provider; the preset mounts only the model-facing web tool. Its lowercase `memory.md` is a bounded 16 KiB reference index: missing context receives the full index, while later file edits produce a short stale-copy notice with current usage, not another full copy. Identity, ownership, and Workspace participation update separately; [Member context injection](../../docs/team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md#member-context-injection) defines recovery. `notes/` stays on-demand through filesystem tools. Over-budget indexes receive a maintenance warning, not silent truncation. Ordinary sessions and forks receive no Team identity or private-memory context. At Host startup every enabled Member's private memory is provisioned and an `inactive` Member's is removed with its Session archived; directories the replayed ledger does not reference are never pruned, so leftovers from a discarded ledger stay on disk for the operator. Both that removal and the activation-time migration of a pre-fix colon directory act only on paths inside the running process's own `$DSH_HOME/agent-team/members/`: a recorded path naming a different DSH home (an isolated test home, a second instance) is refused with a warning rather than renamed or deleted, because acting on it would take a Member's real private memory out of its home.
32	
33	Adding a Member to a Project grants future read/send/claim authority but injects no historical Messages into the member session. A Thread is created by `startThread`, never by a Main stream message: a started Thread is a discussion, or a Task when `kind: 'task'` asks for one, and a Human can later promote a taskless Thread by atomically adding its Task overlay and a structured `promote` Task activity. Thread Attention starts when a Thread is created, a Claim is created, or a member follows — never from a mention or a reply, which deliver one direct marker and leave Attention alone. Ordinary unread is derived from Attention; structured mentions create durable direct markers, while terminal Task changes retain sparse Activity markers for affected followers after Attention ends. `team_inbox` and Thread reads are Host projections, not Session inbox contents. A direct mention context includes its Message body and source; Task/Claim changes — including promotion — include the complete immutable event; ordinary unread carries a body-free Thread-first route. Pending hints are coalesced, ignored hints do not loop, and resume/error recovery derives a new hint from durable unread state. For recoverable service failures, the Host wakes a Member after each of the first two consecutive `agent/error` occurrences, then leaves the third failure for the operator; only a clean turn resets that run.
34	
35	Member replies require the exact current Thread revision and atomically update Message and Thread facts. `threadRef` is the primary collaboration identity; the Host also resolves `taskRef` to its taskful Thread, while Task/Claim operations remain Task-ref based. Each tool action's address requirements are defined in the [tool contract](../../docs/team-collaboration/tools.md). [Mutation fences](../../docs/team-collaboration/boundaries.md#mutation-fences) defines the unread and revision checks: exact, complete Thread Message and Activity facts from a Team notice or tool result can satisfy the context requirement without acknowledging unread. A Main stream post has no token and follows the same context rule. A DM cannot supply Thread evidence. Complete rejections can support reconsideration; partial results require reading. A closed Task rejects replies and new Attention; reopening restores the Task without restoring prior Attention. Taskless Threads still support replies, follow, mentions, Inbox, read, and history, but have no Claims or Task-resolution path. Under rules version 2 a mention delivers one direct marker and never starts Attention, and a reply carries the parent's author into the recipient set the same way. Every addressable recipient is delivered — a Member the Thread has never carried included — and nothing follows as a side effect; there is no invitation step and no undelivered remainder to report. Mentions are authored in the Message body as `@Handle` and resolved by the Host against the Project's addressable names; the body is the sole delivery authority, and no recipient list travels with the request. Message facts carry the resolved refs, and the Client renders mention chips only for those Members. Claim/done/release and Task changes are ordered host-authored Activities. Active Claims exclude only the same normalized Direction; different Directions can run concurrently. Task state is derived from Claims unless Human acceptance or closure overrides it. Close releases active Claims and clears Thread Attention atomically. Member removal marks the member inactive, releases owned active Claims, clears its Attention and direct markers, and archives the session after the durable commit. Message and Activity facts share one bounded sequence cursor.
36	
37	`changes({ scope? }, signal?)` returns an `AsyncIterable<{ version: number }>` through a streaming Remote. It emits the current baseline, then matching workspace/project/thread/presence invalidations; omitting scope observes shared projections but not presence. A paused consumer retains only the latest pending version; cancellation or Host disposal closes the stream. The Client must reread projections on every baseline, even when the version is unchanged or lower after a restart. See [architecture](../../docs/architecture/host-authority.md) for scope/version and recovery semantics. Thread reads change only private read state: they wake no scope, and a read with no unread or markers to consume appends no operation. After a commit, Inbox hints are recomputed only for affected Members.
38	
39	Agent Thread and Main stream reads restore missing original background from current Session visibility, explicitly omit already-visible Message bodies and complete Activity events, and acknowledge only the prefix the tool can render within its output ceiling; a Thread read receipt stores that bound, while older receipts keep the default batch. Long bodies return in ordered parts, and repeating the same request resumes at the missing segment. Human reads, Remote parameters, and durable receipt interpretation are otherwise unchanged; [the reading contract](../../docs/team-collaboration/tools.md#team_thread) defines the presentation.
40	
41	M1 supports one Host writer. The ledger is permanent and has no snapshot or compaction path.
42	
43	## Composition
44	
45	The bundle consumes the Host's existing singleton providers; it does not mount replacements for `agents`, default model selection, `tools`, `fs`, `sandboxPolicy`, Session store/persistence, or Workspace registry. Its private SQLite DomainFacility does not replace the Host's global storage service, so toggling the bundle does not rebuild unrelated storage consumers. Load those Host services once, then mount this Service and its invariant companion. The Team Web Client is the only Human control surface.
46	
47	A team-enabled preset registers the seven tools in its own agent scope and marks the `team_message` definition with `markAgentTeamPreset()`. Preset rows must resolve `ctx.agentTeam` when executing, not statically inject it: the Host mounts member presets while it restores Members during its own activation, so a row that declares `agentTeam` as a dependency cannot activate and fails every startup restore. Duplicate scoped tool names fail during unpublished setup and make only that Member unavailable. Duplicate Host service providers remain a composition error and should be removed rather than layered.
48	
49	Member context has two mechanisms and no model tool. The preset's `member-compaction-engine` delegates summaries and durable reduction to the Harness, while Team bounds input and output before each request; [`../../docs/team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md`](../../docs/team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md) owns those numbers. A generation swap is a Host decision at a wake boundary: `team-context-management.ts` waits for true idle, rechecks the owned-jobs guard, commits the idempotent `team/member-session-recycled` operation (Host actor), retires the old Session (dispose and archive, never delete), and activates a fresh one parented at the one it replaces. Identity, model, private memory, skills, Claims, and Attention survive, and process state is reconstructible from the durable log after a crash. No Remote write renews, rolls over, or otherwise resets a Member's context.
50	
51	## Model Experience
52	
53	### Host collaboration state
54	
55	#### What the model sees
56	
57	An enabled Member may receive one bounded, coalesced context notification after durable unread work appears. Structured direct mentions include their Message body and source; Task/Claim Activities include their complete immutable event; ordinary unread includes only a Thread-first route and counts, with a Task overlay where present. The notification is queued at the Agent's safe step boundary, so active model requests and tools are not interrupted. It routes the common path directly to `team_thread.read`; the model uses `team_inbox` only when it needs to triage remaining Threads. Missing direct signals are ranked ahead of ordinary counts; [`../../docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md`](../../docs/team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md) owns the notice shape, order, and budget.
58	
59	#### Token effect
60	
61	The ledger, projection, and Human status reads add no model tokens.
62	
63	#### KV Cache effect
64	
65	The Host ledger and Human status reads do not alter model requests or cache reuse.
66	
67	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
68	
69	- **Single Host writer** — concurrent processes over one dshHome are unsupported; operation serialization is process-local.
70	- **Permanent ledger** — M1 provides neither snapshots nor compaction, so storage grows with committed collaboration facts.
71	- **No remote provider seam** — the package combines the capability definition and its only implementation until a real remote Consumer requires another Provider.
72	- **No Session migration of its own** — Member Sessions ride the Host's Session persistence and its released-format migration chain; this package provides no Team ledger or Member Session migration, compatibility read, or fallback.
73

CHANGELOG.md:29:- Event-evaluated Task reminders cover review backlog and stalled work. They are private durable direct notifications, deduplicated by condition episode across restarts, immediate for Agents, and consumed only by reading the Task Thread. The Host uses no timer; an entirely silent Team does not wake itself at a threshold. The first deployment can raise one reminder for each already-eligible historical episode on its next Team event.
CHANGELOG.md:36:- Complete Thread Message rejections provide the facts and current token needed to reconsider a write without a mandatory extra read. The Host verifies exact Team source, Thread/Message identity, and the actual Session text; summaries and truncated results cannot satisfy the check. Partial rejections supply no token, and neither notifications nor rejections acknowledge unread work.
CHANGELOG.md:57:- The follow control reads the Human's own row out of the follower set instead of asking whether the set is non-empty. The set holds every Member whose Attention is on the Thread, so while any Agent still followed, the Human's unfollow left the button pressed with the pressed fill while its word read 「关注」; the same reading also made a press on a Thread only an Agent followed answer "already following". The Human's own Attention and notification gate were never wrong — only the Client's identity test was.
CHANGELOG.md:86:- A cold Member generation is replaced automatically before a wake reaches it. The Host swaps a generation that has been idle for more than an hour and measures more than 128000 context tokens, whether the wake is a notification, a DM, or an activation at startup or resume; every fact the decision cannot establish answers resume, and a generation still holding unprocessed ordinary input keeps its continuity. Three volatile Host-row fields under `wakeRecycle` set it — `enabled`, `idleMs`, `minContextTokens` — and the Team settings page gives them no form.
CHANGELOG.md:87:- A swap no longer strands the input it was racing. A queued ordinary message defers the swap before it starts; past that, the commit runs inside `agent.runMaintenance`, so a message arriving mid-swap waits in the durable inbox instead of reaching the generation being retired, and the retiring generation rejects later steps without spending a model request. Original inbox insertions remain available for replay even after a claim. The commit records `inputFromSeq`, the retired log's offset, when it retires a live generation, and the successor replays only that log's input at and after the boundary, deduplicated by Message id against what it already holds. Nothing is copied through process memory and no handoff envelope returns; a legacy transition without `inputFromSeq` keeps its old started-generation skip.
CHANGELOG.md:235:- Fixed archived Channels leaking their Threads into the Inbox: archival ends participation as well as notification.
CHANGELOG.md:295:- Fixed early-accept notifications carrying an empty finished-claim clause.

Durable unread changes may produce one bounded coalesced Agent context notification through the public safe boundary: direct mentions carry their Message and source, Task/Claim Activities carry the complete event (actor, object, Claim refs or transfer endpoints), and ordinary unread carries only a body-free Thread-first route. - The notice ranks missing direct signals before reminders and ordinary counts; [attention-and-messaging.md](../team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md) owns its order, caps, and character budget.
- A committed Session transition (`team/member-session-renewed`, `team/member-session-rolled-over`, `team/member-session-recycled`) records the desired binding, not a completed one: retiring the old generation and activating the target are Host effects outside the ledger write. Startup and the explicit Member recovery action both finish an interrupted transition from the recorded previous Session, and each effect derives its own completion — a live handle never proves the archive half ran. A repeated request answers with the recorded receipt and an honest status, never a second binding.
- Every durable Member state has one desired external effect set — the [Member Lifecycle](../domain-model.md#member-lifecycle) table. Each lifecycle operation re-runs that set right after its commit, and startup re-runs it for every non-enabled Member, so an archive, suspension, or removal interrupted by a crash or a failed Workspace/Session/filesystem call converges by repeating the same derivation rather than by a second durable write.
- Startup never activates a non-enabled Member: an effect that fails during startup is logged and retried at the next boot instead of failing the boot. Lifecycle operations for one Member stay serialized in submission order, while different Members never queue behind each other's waits.
- Task reminders are Host-owned `team/reminder-raised` operations evaluated after Team events, never timers. Their optional `reminderMarkers` Inbox delta is private to one recipient; replay retains the complete episode for deduplication after its marker is consumed.
- Reminder operations invalidate the Task Thread change scope so the Human Inbox refreshes, but add no public fact or revision. Acceptance, close, and lifecycle cleanup remove obsolete unread markers while retaining episode history. Agent idle observations are process-local, retained across generation replacement and discarded on Host restart; unknown idle never satisfies a time condition.

A failed Inbox wake clears its recorded notice state, so the next commit touching that Member rederives the same durable Inbox facts and retries without a second append. DM keeps its explicit recorded-but-not-delivered error.

23	- Agent lifecycle、JSON/SQLite replay、authorization、idempotency 和 revision checks 都留在 Host 侧。durable unread 变化可以通过 public Agent safe-boundary API 产生一条有界、合并的 Agent context notification。direct mentions 携带 Message 和 source。Task/Claim Activities 携带完整事件——actor、对象、Claim refs 或 transfer 两端。ordinary unread 只携带不含正文的 Thread-first route，存在 Task 时再带 Task overlay。Promotion 与其他 Task transition 一样是 Task activity，通过 Activity markers 到达 followers。notification 不是第二权威，也不保证模型恰好处理一次。
24	- 通知先排缺失的 direct 信号，再排 reminder 与普通计数；其排序、上限和字符预算见 [attention-and-messaging.zh.md](../team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.zh.md)。
25	- 已提交的 Session transition（`team/member-session-renewed`、`team/member-session-rolled-over`、`team/member-session-recycled`）记录的是 desired binding，而不是已完成的切换。retire 旧代与 activate 目标都是 ledger 写入之外的 Host 效果。startup 与 Member 的显式 recovery 动作都会补完被中断的 transition，依据记录的 previous Session。每个效果各自推导自己是否已完成。live handle 不能证明 archive 那一半跑过。重复请求只返回已记录的 receipt 与诚实状态，不再提交一次绑定。
26	- 每个 durable Member state 只有一组期望的外部 effect，即 [Member Lifecycle](../domain-model.zh.md#member-lifecycle) 表。每一次 lifecycle operation 在 commit 之后重跑这组 effect。startup 对每个非 enabled Member 也重跑同一组。archive、suspension、remove 因此走同一条推导重跑收敛，不做第二次 durable 写入。即使 Workspace/Session/filesystem 调用被 crash 或失败打断，也一样收敛。
27	- startup 绝不把非 enabled Member 激活为 enabled。启动阶段失败的 effect 只记日志，下一次 boot 重试，不让 boot 失败。同一 Member 的 lifecycle operation 按提交序串行；不同 Member 从不排在彼此的等待之后。
28	- Task 提醒由 Host 在 Team 事件后评估并写入 `team/reminder-raised`，不使用 timer。其可选 `reminderMarkers` Inbox delta 仅属于一个接收者；marker 被读取消费后，replay 仍保留完整 episode 用于去重。
29	- reminder operation 会使对应 Task Thread 的 change scope 失效，让 Human Inbox 刷新，但不增加公开 fact 或 revision。accept、close 与生命周期清理会移除已经失效的未读 marker，同时保留 episode 历史。Agent idle 是进程内观测，跨 generation 替换保留，Host 重启后丢弃；idle 未知时不满足时间条件。
30	
31	- ledger append 之后剩下的是 delivery 效果：commit listeners、Client change invalidation、participation notice。每个受影响的 Member 还会收到一次 wake。每一项都经过同一条边界：普通失败只记日志，不让操作本身失败，调用方仍收到 committed result。
32	- 同步执行的 invariant divergence 仍会让调用方收到 reject；延迟通知中的 divergence 因 commit 已经返回，只记 error 级日志。失败的 Inbox wake 清掉这个 wake 记录的 notice state。因此，下一次触及该 Member 的 commit 重新推导同一批 durable Inbox facts 并重试，不追加第二次操作。DM 保留显式的 recorded-but-not-delivered 错误。

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file. The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and Semantic Versioning. Team bundle versions evolve independently of DeepSeek Harness versions; DeepSeek Harness compatibility is expressed through `peerDependencies` and [`docs/dsh-release-compatibility.md`](docs/dsh-release-compatibility.md).
4	
5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	**Upgrade note**
8	
9	- Rules version 2 is now the default and the `DSH_AGENT_TEAM_PREVIEW_RULES` preview switch is gone: this build adopts version 2 on every ledger it opens and no longer writes the version 1 kinds it replaced (`team/message-sent`; they replay inside version 1 segments only). A build at or below 0.2.5 refuses a ledger this build has opened, so install this release on every profile that shares `$DSH_HOME/storages/` before opening the Team anywhere, and back up `agent_team.sqlite` first. Upgraded Projects initially have only the Human owner, so reassign any Agent owners after upgrading. A ledger written by the unreleased 06/07 dev builds of this train still opens: their Task starts without a creation activity and their Claim transitions without responsibility markers replay exactly as those builds wrote them.
10	
11	**New**
12	
13	- Tasks carry one accountable owner. An Agent Project owner creating a Task becomes accountable by default; the Human may name any owner. Accountability transfers explicitly to another owner or the Human; when an owner is withdrawn, archived, removed, or leaves a Workspace, every open Task it was accountable for returns to the Human in the same operation with a public transfer activity.
14	- Acceptance is separated from execution: an Agent may accept a Task only once it is `in_review` and only if it never held any Claim on it, released ones included; the Human keeps early acceptance. Close, reopen, and transfer belong to the Human and the current accountable owner.
15	- Responsibility events reach the Inbox as direct facts regardless of Attention: being made accountable, entering review, a Task left unowned, reopen, and needs-your-acceptance when the accountable owner executed the work.
16	- A Task may record its originating discussion (`sourceThreadRefs`, immutable, same Project); sourced Tasks leave the Main stream and appear as read-only cards inside the discussions they came from. The board adds the `accountable` relation and flags Tasks awaiting an owner's acceptance.
17	- `team_task` gains `accept`, `close`, `reopen`, and `transfer`; `team_message.start` accepts an accountable owner and source discussions for Tasks. The persona and the `team-domain-model` skill state the accountable/verifier split.
18	- The team-member persona separates naming from mentioning: a Member referred to in plain prose — Iris, Ferry — is a reference, while `@Handle` in a Message body is a delivery, so a stray `@` inside a roster explanation or a quoted report no longer interrupts Members who need not act on it.
19	- Notices are delivered by Attention. Every unread fact interrupts: a Main stream post, a new discussion, mentions, replies, ownership events, responsibility events and Task reminders wake immediately, and so does an ordinary Thread update for any Member following that Thread. The former owner and accountable threshold — five ordinary Thread updates per Member per Thread before a summary — is gone, so following a Thread now means being interrupted by its first ordinary update, and no identity places a reader in a slower class. The sender's own messages never enter the sender's Inbox.
20	- A Main stream commit wakes every Member whose Main stream Attention covers that stream, not only the Project's owners, so a non-owner follower is interrupted by the first ordinary update like anyone else. Following a Main stream requires Project membership, exactly as reading and writing it do, so an Attention row left behind by a departed Member delivers nothing and the follow cannot be the door that gets a Member in.
21	- An ownership grant no longer overwrites the Main stream Attention a Member already holds: a Member that followed and read before being granted ownership keeps its own read watermark, so granting ownership no longer silently clears its unread. The Human's own row is derived from owning the Project, so a Main stream unfollow from the Human is refused instead of committing an operation that changes nothing; `team_attention` takes `projectRef` or a Thread ref, never both, at the Host as well as the tool.
22	- A Thread the notice cannot render — the section cap or the character budget dropped it — keeps its facts undelivered, so the next relevant commit rederives and retries them instead of leaving them swallowed by a notice that never named them.
23	- An Attention row records what established it — starting the Thread, claiming its Task, being its accountable, owning the Project, being named in it, or choosing to follow — so a result can state why the reader follows instead of guessing. `team_attention` renders the cause once the reader follows, and a Claim result or a Thread start names the Attention it just established. The source is optional in storage: rows written before it existed keep their bytes; replay derives the missing cause from the operation that wrote the row and then validates the repaired projection strictly.
24	- The Main stream carries its own Attention, keyed by Member × Project and independent of any Thread's row, so ordinary Main stream unread no longer follows from owning the Project. The Human's row is derived from the Project's creation and only its read watermark is stored; an Agent's is written by the ownership grant, starting at the grant sequence so no historical backlog is inherited; any other Member's comes from an explicit follow. A Member that does not follow the Main stream holds markers alone — a mention or a reply still reaches it — and withdrawing ownership keeps the row, so the Member keeps its ordinary unread until it reads or unfollows. The Main stream standing's `owner` field is replaced by `following`.
25	- `team_attention` takes `projectRef` to follow or unfollow a Project's Main stream, mutually exclusive with `threadRef`/`taskRef`. 26	- Every visible Project carries one Main stream unread row in the Inbox, shared by the Human and Agents; `team_inbox` and the Human's inbox count agree.

29	- Event-evaluated Task reminders cover review backlog and stalled work. 30	- Agent `team_thread` renders a discussion's derived Task cards with current status and accountable owner. Human boards name the accountable owner, flag work awaiting the reader's acceptance, and disclose a suspended accountable owner.
31	
32	**Changed**
33	
34	- Agent Thread and Main stream reads restore missing original discussion context even after compaction with no unread. Already-visible Message bodies are explicitly omitted while the read acknowledges the same chronological batch; background, Main stream Thread cards, and current Task cards remain separate from newly acknowledged facts. Human reads and historical read receipts are unchanged.

1	# Team 性能评测
2	
3	[English](team-performance.md) | 中文
4	
5	## 目的
6	
7	Team 性能评测覆盖加载、tool call、ledger 读取、Session 工作和协作流程，测量 Human 或 Member 可以观察到的成本。它是评测工具，不是生产运行路径，只有显式开启后才运行。
8	
9	场景源码位于 [`scripts/team-performance/`](../../scripts/team-performance/)。入口和输出格式见 [`scripts/README.md`](../../scripts/README.md)。
10	
11	## 运行评测
12	
13	### 基线
14	
15	在一个 Node 进程中运行默认 16 个场景：
16	
17	```sh
18	DSH_BENCH_TEAM=1 npm run bench:team
19	```
20	
21	命令在 `artifacts/team-perf/runs/` 下写入一次运行目录，包含 `manifest.json`、测量样本 `samples.jsonl` 和 `summary.json`。默认使用 3 个测量样本和 1 个 warmup。用 `DSH_BENCH_SCENARIOS` 选择场景，用 `DSH_BENCH_THREADS`、`DSH_BENCH_FOLLOWERS`、`DSH_BENCH_MEMBERS`、`DSH_BENCH_SESSION_EVENTS` 等对应变量调整负载规模。
22	
23	### 规模矩阵
24	
25	在独立 Node 进程中运行默认 15 个 case：
26	
27	```sh
28	npm run bench:team:matrix
29	```
30	
31	用逗号分隔的 `scenario:threads:followers` 设置 `DSH_BENCH_MATRIX_CASES`。默认协作 case 覆盖真实数据中的 1–4 个 follower、8 个 Member 的队列边界、20 个 Thread 的积压，以及一个 32 follower 压力 case。当场景需要时，矩阵 runner 会把第一个规模值路由给 Member 或 Session 负载。每个矩阵目录包含 manifest、子运行目录和汇总的 `results.json`。
32	
33	### 真实 profile 使用情况
34	
35	从真实 profile 的 SQLite 只读副本汇总使用情况：
36	
37	```sh
38	npm run bench:team:usage -- /path/to/agent_team.sqlite --json
39	```
40	
41	报告统计 operation、Member、Thread Attention 规模、回复影响人数，以及接近通知队列阈值的 operation。它读取原始 operation，不强制使用当前 ledger replay，因此旧的 `team/channel-*` 记录仍可统计。
42	
43	受影响 Member 数是估算值：包含持久化 Inbox 接收者、每次 operation 后的 Thread Attention 和 actor，但不包含 Main stream 接收者推导。报告只输出计数，不输出 Message 正文或 handle。
44	
45	### Browser 加载
46	
47	测量组装后的 Web bundle 和 Team mode：
48	
49	```sh
50	DSH_BENCH_BROWSER_SAMPLES=3 npm run bench:team:browser
51	```
52	
53	每个样本使用新的临时 Web scaffold 和 Chromium。runner 记录页面加载、Workspace connection、普通界面 ready、Team mode ready、导航计时、传输字节数、console warning 和 page error。结果写在 `artifacts/team-perf/browser/runs/` 下的 `manifest.json`、`samples.jsonl` 和 `summary.json`。Browser 结果必须同时看 p95、p99 和单个样本，因为冷启动方差明显。
54	
55	### 语义探针
56	
57	检查 commit 后有序通知队列：
58	
59	```sh
60	DSH_BENCH_TEAM=1 npm run bench:team:semantics
61	```
62	
63	探针检查投递失败重试、按 Member 的顺序、通知 drain 前的 Client invalidation、关闭取消和 dispose 错误。时间评测通过不能代替这些检查。
64	
65	### 比较运行结果
66	
67	比较两次基线 summary 或两个矩阵结果文件：
68	
69	```sh
70	npm run bench:team:compare -- before/summary.json after/summary.json
71	npm run bench:team:compare -- --max-regression 20 before/summary.json after/summary.json
72	```
73	
74	比较器输出共同场景的 p50、p95、p99，并单独报告缺失场景、缺失指标和无效测量。指定 `--max-regression` 时，没有有效分位数的指标会使比较失败，零基线变为正值也会失败，不再被当作无法比较。只有负载、环境和场景 schema 相同，回归阈值才有意义。
75	
76	## 场景覆盖
77	
78	| 范围 | 场景 | 主要证据 |
79	| --- | --- | --- |
80	| 加载与激活 | `bundle-size`、`host-boot`、`member-activation`、`member-activation-batch`、`member-resume` | bundle 字节数、Host fixture boot、新 Member 和已有 Member 激活、顺序与并发激活 |
81	| Tool 路径 | `tool-call`、`tool-read-sweep`、`thread-read-reply`、`tool-write`、`notification-retry` | tool 总耗时、Host handler 耗时、结果字节数、读写和失败投递恢复 |
82	| 协作 | `collaboration-fanout`、`collaboration-agent-turn` | durable commit、Ledger queue wait/service、fan-out dispatch、事件循环延迟、通知 drain、模型请求和 idle 阶段 |
83	| Session 与存储 | `session-fold`、`session-replay-jsonl`、`ledger-read-memory`、`ledger-replay-sqlite` | cursor 和 projection fold、JSONL 写入/读取/字节数、受限 ledger 读取、SQLite 打开/replay/校验 |
84	
85	基线使用真实 Team Host fixture；需要模型回合时使用确定性的 model adapter。它不代表生产模型提供方或某一台用户机器。Browser 场景检查组装后的完整路径，Node 场景解释该路径内部的成本。
86	
87	## 当前约束
88	
89	- 通知读取材料只在一次投递尝试内复用。Facts、delivery plan 和 projection 不形成长期缓存，也不形成第二个 authority。
90	- 一次提交影响至少 8 个 Member 时，通知 effect 在 durable commit 和 Client invalidation 后进入队列。每个 Member 内保持顺序，不同 Member 独立调度。关闭开始时尚未开始的 effect 会跳过；下一次 activation 会重新从 durable unread facts 派生。
91	- JSONL 生产默认仍是 `zstd`。在当前 fixture 中，无压缩 replay 更快，但占用明显更多磁盘空间。
92	- 当前测得的批量 Member activation 已经从并发调用中获益。仅凭这一结果不能改变 Host startup 的恢复顺序，还需要单独的启动恢复实验。
93	- Browser 冷启动有明显长尾。保留样本记录并比较分布，不要把一次运行变成硬性验收阈值。
94	
95	## 改动流程
96	
97	改动性能敏感路径时，先运行能观察该改动的最小场景，再运行相关规模 case 和语义探针。前后比较必须使用相同场景。墙钟数据要和 operation 数、结果形状一起检查；耗时下降但事实缺失的结果应视为失败。把结果视为已交付前，运行 `npm test` 和 `npm run check:artifact`。
98	
99	不要把密钥、真实 profile 或临时 browser overlay 放进仓库。评测默认关闭，所以普通开发和发布检查不会运行它。
100

受影响 Member 数是估算值：包含持久化 Inbox 接收者、每次 operation 后的 Thread Attention 和 actor，但不包含 Main stream 接收者推导。报告只输出计数，不输出 Message 正文或 handle。

### Browser 加载

测量组装后的 Web bundle 和 Team mode：

```sh
DSH_BENCH_BROWSER_SAMPLES=3 npm run bench:team:browser
```

每个样本使用新的临时 Web scaffold 和 Chromium。runner 记录页面加载、Workspace connection、普通界面 ready、Team mode ready、导航计时、传输字节数、console warning 和 page error。结果写在 `artifacts/team-perf/browser/runs/` 下的 `manifest.json`、`samples.jsonl` 和 `summary.json`。Browser 结果必须同时看 p95、p99 和单个样本，因为冷启动方差明显。

### 语义探针

检查 commit 后有序通知队列：

```sh
DSH_BENCH_TEAM=1 npm run bench:team:semantics
```

探针检查投递失败重试、按 Member 的顺序、通知 drain 前的 Client invalidation、关闭取消和 dispose 错误。时间评测通过不能代替这些检查。

### 比较运行结果

比较两次基线 summary 或两个矩阵结果文件：

```sh
npm run bench:team:compare -- before/summary.json after/summary.json
npm run bench:team:compare -- --max-regression 20 before/summary.json after/summary.json
```

比较器输出共同场景的 p50、p95、p99，并单独报告缺失场景、缺失指标和无效测量。指定 `--max-regression` 时，没有有效分位数的指标会使比较失败，零基线变为正值也会失败，不再被当作无法比较。只有负载、环境和场景 schema 相同，回归阈值才有意义。

## 场景覆盖

| 范围 | 场景 | 主要证据 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 加载与激活 | `bundle-size`、`host-boot`、`member-activation`、`member-activation-batch`、`member-resume` | bundle 字节数、Host fixture boot、新 Member 和已有 Member 激活、顺序与并发激活 |
| Tool 路径 | `tool-call`、`tool-read-sweep`、`thread-read-reply`、`tool-write`、`notification-retry` | tool 总耗时、Host handler 耗时、结果字节数、读写和失败投递恢复 |
| 协作 | `collaboration-fanout`、`collaboration-agent-turn` | durable commit、Ledger queue wait/service、fan-out dispatch、事件循环延迟、通知 drain、模型请求和 idle 阶段 |
| Session 与存储 | `session-fold`、`session-replay-jsonl`、`ledger-read-memory`、`ledger-replay-sqlite` | cursor 和 projection fold、JSONL 写入/读取/字节数、受限 ledger 读取、SQLite 打开/replay/校验 |

基线使用真实 Team Host fixture；需要模型回合时使用确定性的 model adapter。它不代表生产模型提供方或某一台用户机器。Browser 场景检查组装后的完整路径，Node 场景解释该路径内部的成本。

## 当前约束

- 通知读取材料只在一次投递尝试内复用。Facts、delivery plan 和 projection 不形成长期缓存，也不形成第二个 authority。
- 一次提交影响至少 8 个 Member 时，通知 effect 在 durable commit 和 Client invalidation 后进入队列。每个 Member 内保持顺序，不同 Member 独立调度。关闭开始时尚未开始的 effect 会跳过；下一次 activation 会重新从 durable unread facts 派生。
- JSONL 生产默认仍是 `zstd`。在当前 fixture 中，无压缩 replay 更快，但占用明显更多磁盘空间。
- 当前测得的批量 Member activation 已经从并发调用中获益。仅凭这一结果不能改变 Host startup 的恢复顺序，还需要单独的启动恢复实验。
- Browser 冷启动有明显长尾。保留样本记录并比较分布，不要把一次运行变成硬性验收阈值。

## 改动流程

改动性能敏感路径时，先运行能观察该改动的最小场景，再运行相关规模 case 和语义探针。前后比较必须使用相同场景。墙钟数据要和 operation 数、结果形状一起检查；耗时下降但事实缺失的结果应视为失败。把结果视为已交付前，运行 `npm test` 和 `npm run check:artifact`。

不要把密钥、真实 profile 或临时 browser overlay 放进仓库。评测默认关闭，所以普通开发和发布检查不会运行它。

37	`changes({ scope? }, signal?)` 通过流式 Remote 返回 `AsyncIterable<{ version: number }>`。先发送当前基线，之后发送匹配的 workspace/project/thread/presence 通知；省略 scope 时观察共享投影，不包含 presence。消费者暂停期间只保留最新待发送版本；取消或 Host 释放时关闭流。Client 必须在每次基线到达时重读投影，即使重启后的版本相同或更低。scope、版本和恢复语义见[架构文档](../../docs/architecture/host-authority.zh.md)。Thread read 只改变私有已读状态，不唤醒任何 scope；没有未读或 marker 可消费时不追加 operation。提交后只为受影响的 Members 重算 Inbox hints。
38	
39	Agent 的 Thread 与 Main stream read 根据当前 Session 可见性恢复缺失的背景原文，明确省略已可见 Message 正文与完整 Activity 事件，并只确认工具能在输出上限内渲染的前缀；Thread read receipt 记录这个界限，旧 receipt 仍按缺省 batch 解释。超长正文按有序分段返回，重复同一请求从缺失段继续。Human read、Remote 参数与持久 receipt 的解释其余不变；呈现规则见[读取契约](../../docs/team-collaboration/tools.zh.md#team_thread)。
40	
41	M1 支持单个 Host writer。Ledger 永久保留，不提供 snapshot 或 compaction。

## 沟通规范

- 说人话，拒绝行业黑话、互联网黑话。
- 简洁优先。
- 只问真正需要用户拍板的问题。
- 模仿用户的表达方式。

## 文档与报告写作规范

适用于结构化文档与报告（故障报告、分析、清单等）；日常对话遵循“沟通规范”。

- 使用标准术语；已有通用说法时直接采用。
- 直接陈述，让读者无需推断指代对象；用字面表述代替比喻。
- 表头和分类名使用中性名词，如“问题”“现象”“影响”“结果”。
- 直接陈述结论或定义。
- 表格条目按需填写，说明发生了什么即可；数字和结论在有把握时给出。
- 未查明原因的问题写“原因未查明”。
- 使用正式、客观的表述。

## UI / UX 改动

- 涉及界面或交互改动时，用 ASCII UI 展示示意。

## 向用户汇报

用简单直白的语言说清楚：做了什么、结果怎样。

- 把术语和技术细节转成日常语言。
- 像在跟一个聪明人解释，对方没在看代码。
- 干活过程怎么都行；这条要求只针对汇报方式。

## 自验

在汇报前，先用实际工具验证工作结果：

- 能运行就运行，检查输出。
- Web 类：打开页面走一遍流程，确认渲染和交互正常。
- 脚本：拿真实输入跑，检查结果。
- 边界情况也试一遍。

发现问题就先修好，交付能用的成果，让用户拿到就能用。

## 完成标准

- 动手前先想清楚：任务做到什么程度才算完成。
- 先给自己列检查清单。
- 只有确认一切正常，或者真的遇到需要用户介入的障碍，才来找用户。

## 工具使用偏好

- 涉及 GitHub 的操作（查源码、读文件、发 API 请求、查 PR/Issue）优先用 `gh`。

## 方案与决策默认规则

private notificationReadSet: {
  readonly memberId: AgentTeamMemberId
  readonly facts: Map<AgentTeamThreadRef, readonly AgentTeamThreadReadFact[]>
  readonly main: Map<AgentTeamProjectRef, readonly MainUnreadItem[]>
} | undefined

notificationSnapshot(memberId: AgentTeamMemberId): {
  readonly threads: ReturnType<AgentTeamLedger['notificationFacts']>
  readonly main: ReturnType<AgentTeamLedger['mainNotificationFacts']>
} {
  return this.withNotificationReadSet(memberId, () => ({
    threads: this.notificationFacts(memberId),
    main: this.mainNotificationFacts(memberId),
  }))
}

private withNotificationReadSet<T>(memberId: AgentTeamMemberId, read: () => T): T {
  const previous = this.notificationReadSet
  if (previous?.memberId === memberId) return read()
  this.notificationReadSet = { memberId, facts: new Map(), main: new Map() }
  try {
    return read()
  } finally {
    this.notificationReadSet = previous
  }
}

### `packages/agent-team/src/index.ts`

当前队列核心：
```ts
private readonly notificationEffectTails =
  new Map<AgentTeamMemberId, Promise<void>>()

private afterCommit(
  label: string,
  effect: () => void,
  deferNotification = false,
  notificationMemberId?: AgentTeamMemberId,
): void {
  const pendingNotification = notificationMemberId === undefined
    ? undefined
    : this.notificationEffectTails.get(notificationMemberId)

  if (notificationMemberId !== undefined &&
      (deferNotification || pendingNotification !== undefined)) {
    const previous = pendingNotification ?? Promise.resolve()
    const queued = previous.then(() => new Promise<void>(resolve => {
      setImmediate(() => {
        try {
          if (this.accepting) effect()
        } catch (error) {
          if (error instanceof AgentTeamInvariantError) {
            this.ctx.logger.error(
              `agent-team: post-commit ${label} violated an invariant: ${error.message}`,
            )
          } else {
            this.ctx.logger.warn(
              `agent-team: post-commit ${label} failed: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`,
            )
          }
        } finally {
          resolve()
        }
      })
    }))
    this.notificationEffectTails.set(notificationMemberId, queued)
    void queued.then(() => {
      if (this.notificationEffectTails.get(notificationMemberId) !== queued) return
      this.notificationEffectTails.delete(notificationMemberId)
    })
    return
  }

  try {
    effect()
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof AgentTeamInvariantError) throw error
    this.ctx.logger.warn(/* ordinary post-commit failure */)
  }
}
```

## Findings

### P2 — 恢复后的 Member 仍被使用统计报告为 suspended

**Location:** `scripts/team-performance/team-live-usage.ts:119–128,146–154`。

**Evidence:** 新脚本依次处理 `member-added`、`member-updated`、`member-archived`、`member-suspended`、`member-removed`，遗漏 `team/member-resumed`。而该操作在 `packages/agent-team/src/types/operations.ts:63–65` 明确携带恢复后的完整 Member。

本轮用真实 `sqliteHarness` 和 `AgentTeamLedger` 创建临时 SQLite，依次执行 `addMember → suspendMember → resumeMember`。关闭写入端后，通过 `team-live-usage.ts <database> --json` 读取。未接触用户真实 profile。

```json
{
  "expected": { "memberState": "enabled", "enabled": 1, "suspended": 0 },
  "actual": { "current": 1, "enabled": 0, "byState": { "suspended": 1 } },
  "operations": {
    "team/initialized": 1,
    "team/member-added": 1,
    "team/member-resumed": 1,
    "team/member-suspended": 1,
    "team/rules-version-adopted": 1
  }
}
```

**Impact:** 有过暂停和恢复、之后没有其他覆盖 Member 快照的操作时，脚本低估 enabled Member 数，并把其 Thread Attention 从 `enabledMembers` 统计中排除。新文档和工作项使用该统计描述日常协作规模，因此相关数字需要修正后重新生成。这不证明当前真实 profile 的具体数字必然有误，但证明脚本不能可靠计算这类历史。

**Basis:** 新性能文档承诺统计真实 profile 的 Member 和 Thread Attention；ticket 01/03 要求测量结果与输入事实一致。源码与真实 ledger 的当前状态是事实依据。

**Suggested fix:** 把 `team/member-resumed` 纳入 Member 状态更新；增加添加、暂停、恢复、归档和移除序列的自动测试，并断言 enabled Member 及 enabled follower 计数。修复后重新生成用于工作项结论的真实 profile 统计。

# Review 02 — Team 性能优化复审

**结论：** 本次复审列出的 5 个问题已处理。工作项仍保留“clean commit 对照、完整性能样本和真实 Agent 工具闭环”等未完成验收项，不把它们误标为已完成。

**复审范围：** 当前工作树中的 Host 通知路径、性能评测脚本、比较器、Harness 路径解析和维护文档。

**复审日期：** 2026-10-30

## Findings 处理结果

| 编号 | 结果 | 处理 | 验证 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | 已处理 | 某 Member 已有延迟通知时，后续小批次也进入同一条 Member 链，不再同步插队；语义探针改为“大批次后小批次”。 | `post-commit-delivery.spec.ts` 12/12；语义探针 ordering 通过，序列为前一提交的 8 次通知后再处理后一提交。 |
| F2 | 已处理 | 比较器把 `count: 0`、缺失分位数和无效测量报告为 invalid；零基线变为正值在 `--max-regression` 下失败。 | equal、普通回归、空测量、零到正值四组 CLI 检查全部符合预期。 |
| F3 | 已处理 | baseline 复用 `scripts/harness-dir.mjs` 的 `harnessDir`，支持相对 checkout、绝对路径和 `.generated-harness` 规则。 | `DSH_HARNESS_DIR=deepseek-harness` smoke 正确记录 Harness commit。 |
| F4 | 已处理 | 注释和 Host authority 双语文档区分同步 invariant reject 与延迟通知 error log；后者不改变已返回的 committed result。 | 文档检查通过；延迟 invariant 测试通过。 |
| F5 | 已处理 | 英文和中文文档索引的 Where to start 增加 Team 性能入口。 | `npm run check:docs` 通过。 |

## 真实使用边界

新增 `bench:team:usage`，读取显式 SQLite 副本的原始 operation 和 Inbox delta，不强制用当前 ledger replay，因此旧的 `team/channel-*` 记录仍可统计。它只输出计数，不输出 Message 正文或 handle。

当前真实 profile 的统计结果为：25,838 条 operation、23 个 enabled Member、483 个 Attention Thread；enabled Member 的 follower 数 p95 为 1、最大 3，全部 durable Attention row 的最大值为 4。Thread write 的受影响 Member 估算 p95 为 3、最大 10；8 人队列阈值命中 103/10,261 次，最近 30 天为 1/2,750 次。历史 8–10 人协作高峰仍然存在，因此异步队列保留为低频保护路径，不继续扩展为常态架构。

默认矩阵已改为 1、2、4、8 follower，20 Thread/4 follower 和 1 Thread/32 follower 压力档。这样日常规模与压力规模分开，避免把 32 follower 的 synthetic 结果解释为普通使用。

## 验证结果

- `npm test`：135 个测试文件通过、1 个跳过；1540 个测试通过、1 个跳过。
- `npm run typecheck`：三个 package 通过。
- `npm run build`：通过。
- `npm run check:artifact`：358 个 artifact entry 通过，65 个 runtime relative import 全部解析。
- `DSH_BENCH_TEAM=1 npm run bench:team:semantics`：failure recovery、shutdown cancellation、mixed-batch ordering、Client invalidation 全部通过。
- `DSH_BENCH_MATRIX_SAMPLES=1 DSH_BENCH_MATRIX_WARMUPS=0 npm run bench:team:matrix`：15/15 case 通过。
- `npm run bench:team:usage -- /home/yu/.dsh/storages/agent_team.sqlite`：真实 live SQLite 只读统计通过。

## deepwiki
DeepWiki MCP provides AI-powered documentation for GitHub repositories.

With a user OAuth token, all devin_* tools act in one organization: without an X-Org-Id header, the first one the user joined. Not found usually means another of their orgs; send X-Org-Id: <org id> to switch.

Available tools:
- read_wiki_structure: Get a list of documentation topics for a repository
- read_wiki_contents: View full documentation about a repository
- ask_wiki_question: Ask any question about a repository's codebase and get an AI-powered answer from its wiki
- list_wiki_repos: List the repositories that have a DeepWiki index (private mode only)
- generate_wiki: Generate a codebase wiki for a repository — only use when explicitly requested by the user (private mode only)
- devin_automation_manage: Manage Devin automations — list, get, create, update, delete, or fetch the trigger event schemas (private mode only)
- devin_billing_tag_manage: Manage Devin billing tags (groupings of Devin sessions for usage tracking) — list, get, create, assign sessions, look up session tags (private mode only)
- devin_blueprint_test: Test a candidate blueprint YAML in an authoring VM: start → run initialize → fix → run initialize again (clean VM) → run maintenance → then persist with update_environment_config (private mode only)
- devin_campaign_manage: Read and publish a bot's campaign documents (plan, readings, status) — get, update, validate (private mode only)
- devin_code_scan_manage: Manage Devin code scans, sometimes referred to as 'security scans' or 'Devin Security Swarm' — list scans, list findings, list profiles, get a profile, create a scan, remediate a finding (private mode only)
- devin_knowledge_manage: Manage Devin knowledge notes and suggestions — list, search, get, create, update, delete notes, view folder structure, list/view/dismiss knowledge suggestions (private mode only)
- devin_mcp_server_manage: Manage org MCP server installations — install (marketplace or custom), update, enable, disable, delete (private mode only)
- devin_oncall_manage: Devin Oncall operations — create and manage Oncall responders (alert, bug report and support request triage), get an Oncall report's current responder membership, page through a responder's open issues, and ingest a dashboard into Oncall knowledge (private mode only)
- devin_playbook_manage: Manage Devin playbooks — list, get, create, update, delete (private mode only)
- devin_review_manage: Trigger a Devin Review for a pull request, fetch the latest review status, or fetch a completed review's findings (private mode only)
- devin_schedule_manage: Manage scheduled Devin sessions — list, get, create, update, delete (private mode only)
- devin_session_create: Create one or more child Devin sessions (private mode only)
- devin_session_interact: Manage a Devin session — get status (one or many sessions, optionally with a short AI summary of each), send messages, sleep/terminate/archive/unarchive, read messages & attachments, manage tags (private mode only)
- devin_session_events: Inspect session events — list summaries, fetch full details, or search event contents (private mode only)
- devin_session_search: Search and filter Devin sessions (private mode only)
- devin_session_insights: Per-session cost, message counts and AI analysis (issues, action items, classification) — list, get, generate (private mode only)
- devin_user_list: List the organization's users by membership kind (direct members or IdP-group members) (private mode only)
- devin_list_integrations: List all native integrations and MCP servers with their status and settings URLs (private mode only)
- devin_find_setting: Find Devin webapp settings pages and deep-link URLs for them (private mode only)
